In casa Inter c'è una situazione non ancora scottante, ma che andrà affrontata quanto prima: il futuro di Marcus Thuram. L'attaccante francese sta vivendo una stagione da protagonista, ma il suo contratto scade il 30 giugno 2028, quando avrà 31 anni: scontata la volontà dei nerazzurri di trattenerlo a Milano, ma difficilmente si potrà imbastire una trattativa alle cifre attuali. Senza dimenticare l'esplosione di Esposito e la clausola rescissoria che permetterebbe all'Inter di far registrare una plusvalenza da record in caso di cessione di Thuram.

La Gazzetta dello Sport prova a fare il punto della situazione: "Thuram ha chiesto più volte ai dirigenti, già nel periodo in cui il direttore sportivo era Piero Ausilio, se esistesse la volontà di proseguire il rapporto insieme. L'Inter ha ovviamente detto che sì, non c'erano dubbi sulle intenzioni e che ci sarebbe stato modo di parlare a tempo debito di un nuovo accordo. [...] Ma il problema di Marcus, classe '97, è proprio questo: quando scadrà il contratto attuale avrà già 31 anni. Come potrebbe la società proporgli oggi un'offerta al rialzo?".

According to recent reports, "Thuram si aspetta di ottenere un aumento di stipendio rispetto ai 6 milioni netti (il decreto crescita aiuta nella tassazione il club) che gli vengono versati adesso. Solo che la politica della sostenibilità imposta da Oaktree ha stabilito che i nuovi contratti debbano prevedere una base fissa non altissima abbinata a una ricca parte mobile: in altre parole, i calciatori devono meritare i loro emolumenti attraverso bonus personali e collettivi determinati dal rendimento. [...] Thuram, per poter restare all'Inter come desidera, dovrà abbassare in modo considerevole le pretese".

"Dalla società filtra ottimismo, oltre alla determinazione di fissare dei paletti finanziari. Però la palla spetta all'interlocutore, di solito bravo a muoverla per gol e assist. Se non si dovesse raggiungere un'intesa, a giugno si potrebbero fare altri ragionamenti: in fondo nell'Inter e nella nazionale italiana si sta affermando un centravanti chiamato Pio Esposito che reclama spazio in attacco. E Thuram ha un certo appeal internazionale, tale da richiamare attenzioni che possono diventare interessamenti concreti: essendo stato ingaggiato a parametro zero, sarebbe una plusvalenza gustosa da valutare.

Sources indicate that piano però con le proiezioni, una postilla sul tema è doverosa: ogni anno, di questi tempi o anche più avanti nella stagione, si parla di possibili offerte per Thuram, che ha una clausola da 85 milioni mai neppure avvicinata da alcuno. E così Marcus è sempre rimasto felicemente a Milano. Anche stavolta la storia potrebbe finire così, magari con un contratto più lungo e meno pesante da ammortizzare per l'Inter".

Sources indicate that gustavo Varela si prepara a diventare uno dei nomi più caldi del mercato di gennaio. Il centravanti portoghese del Monza ha attirato l'interesse di Juventus e Napoli, entrambe alla ricerca di rinforzi per il reparto offensivo. I partenopei lo considerano una possibile alternativa a Lorenzo Lucca, sempre più vicino all'uscita, e hanno iniziato a raccogliere informazioni sul giocatore già da alcune settimane. Anche i bianconeri stanno valutando il profilo, sia in vista della sessione invernale sia per la prossima estate.

La trattativa, però, si presenta tutt'altro che semplice. Il Monza valuta il proprio attaccante almeno 35 milioni di euro, pur potendo prendere in considerazione una cifra leggermente inferiore a fronte di una percentuale sulla futura rivendita. A complicare ulteriormente il quadro c'è la posizione del Benfica, che detiene ancora il 20% dei diritti economici del giocatore: su una valutazione di 35 milioni, circa 7 spetterebbero dunque al club portoghese. I lusitani, inoltre, avrebbero una corsia preferenziale e la possibilità di pareggiare eventuali offerte, elemento che rende più articolata qualsiasi operazione.

It has been revealed that sulle tracce di Gustavo Varela non ci sono soltanto le italiane. Dalla Premier League sono arrivati sondaggi da parte di Liverpool, Tottenham, Brentford e Sunderland, società che possono contare su una disponibilità economica importante. La Juventus potrebbe tentare di costruire un'operazione con una formula più articolata e un investimento dilazionato, ma al momento rischia di partire in svantaggio rispetto alla concorrenza inglese. Il Napoli, invece, dovrà prima definire il futuro di Lucca e capire se ci saranno le condizioni per affondare il colpo sull'attuale capocannoniere di Serie A (9 gol).

#49713. Why Bukayo Saka's England spot is suddenly under threat: Clocking up the miles has made Arsenal star a fitness concern - while his rival Morgan Rogers is hitting top gear: CRAIG HOPE

📅 14 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 6m • 📚 Deep Dive (1279 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚠️ Warning 🌐 Dailymail ↗ Open Full Page

Why Bukayo Saka's England spot is suddenly under threat: Clocking up the miles has made Arsenal star a fitness concern - while his rival Morgan Rogers is hitting top gear: CRAIG HOPE

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1279 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~6 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 08:57 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:21 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Five seasons ago, Bukayo Saka clocked up 3,000 Premier League minutes for Arsenal.
  • Sources indicate that in the same week that Rogers, a Manchester City junior, made his only league start during an unhappy loan season on the south coast - in a goalless draw at Peterborough - Saka was scoring in a 3-1 win in the North London derby.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 08:57 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:21 EST, 14 November 2026.

Five seasons ago, Bukayo Saka clocked up 3,000 Premier League minutes for Arsenal. Morgan Rogers appeared in just 217 for Bournemouth, then of the Championship. The pair are the same school age. Yet, back then, one was a young man at the very top of the game, the other was a boy wondering where, and how, he would ever get a game.

Sources indicate that in the same week that Rogers, a Manchester City junior, made his only league start during an unhappy loan season on the south coast - in a goalless draw at Peterborough - Saka was scoring in a 3-1 win in the North London derby. They were on very different flight paths.

Today, the ascent of Rogers compares with, dare we say it, the gradual descent of Saka. His supporters will contest that trajectory. They can point to his two goals for England in Croatia last month, his hat-trick in the 6-4 World Cup bronze-medal victory over France and, of course, his Premier League winner’s medal. Their argument has merit, as does any that defends a player of such talent.

It has been revealed that except, this is not about ability. It is about durability. It is about mileage and the fear that, at 25 years old, a near 400 career games are weighing heavy. Rogers, quite remarkably, has played 10,000 fewer Premier League minutes. He is, to borrow horse-racing parlance, unexposed and open to improvement.

Recent findings suggest that until three years ago, this was Saka. He started 87 consecutive Premier League games for Arsenal, a club record, and was getting better season on season - seven, 12, 15 and 20 were his goals tallies from 2021 to 2024. He was both the present and future of the England team.

Bukayo Saka's starting spot in the England XI is now under serious threat ahead of Euro 2028.

England are flourishing with Chelsea's Morgan Rogers (right) occupying the right-hand side.

In a recent development, and yet now, increasingly among those who obverse and are close to the England camp - including, you suspect, Thomas Tuchel - there is a feeling of Saka’s presumed starting jersey being under serious threat. In fact, you wonder if the threat has already passed. Does the position on the right of England’s forward line, with a view to Euro 2028, now belong to Rogers?

Sources indicate that this, it should be remarked, is as much about the exceptional development of Rogers, who will again start on the right here in Spain on Sunday night. But there is another, more uncomfortable possibility, and that is of Saka’s very best days belonging to those North London derbies of yesterday, not tomorrow. He is at the moment injured with a thigh strain and faces several more weeks on the sidelines.

I was in the room with Tuchel at the World Cup pre-camp in Florida when he revealed, to some surprise, ’Bukayo is just not there yet. Some things are missing’. We had assumed Saka was fit after arranging private sessions in the wake of the Champions League final. The head coach, however, said it would be ‘very unlikely’ that Saka, nursing Achilles discomfort, would be able to start and finish all of England’s matches, and so it proved. He did not start and finish any before the France kick-about, a match that should have been played at Miami Beach, not Miami Stadium.

Industry observers note that in the days prior to the semi-final against Argentina, Saka told Tuchel and medical staff he was ready to start. Tuchel went with Rogers on the right and Saka was an unused substitute. After his treble three days later, Saka spoke of his frustration with his playing time in North America.

Throughout the tournament, Tuchel rejected the idea of the Arsenal man being ‘the saviour’, as it was put to him by one colleague following the group-stage goalless draw with Ghana.

It has been revealed that ‘I’m not engaging in that,’ he told us. ‘It’s not like Bukayo comes back and everything is solved.’.

In a recent development, and Tuchel was right. Saka did a lot of good - three assists in the tournament proper - but it felt like he was existing in moments, much like at Euro 2024. Gone was that whiplash speed taking him through defensive lines, the drag and dribble that defenders knew was coming but could do little about. Club-mate Noni Madueke had that explosion, just not Saka’s end product. Combine the two and we had a player. It was why, come the semis, Tuchel went with Rogers.

Recurring injuries and setbacks have plagued the Arsenal winger over the past few seasons.

He was once viewed as England's present and future - but has suffered from a gradual decline.

To revisit our Daily Mail Sport tournament ratings, in which Saka scored 6/10, we recorded: ‘Fitness issues should offer some context, but this was a version of Saka unrecognisable from the player we thought was up there with Kane and Bellingham when it came to being a game-changer. He did provide three assists, including a lovely cross for the opener in Mexico, but never appeared to fully trust his body. Has a bit to prove when back to full fitness.’.

It has been revealed that will he ever, though, regain a consistent level of fitness, strength and sharpness that allows him to impact - again, consistently - like he once did? Just last week, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta admitted the club were struggling to identify the underlying reason for injuries which total double figures in three years.

‘We have openly discussed a lot of things with him to understand what could possibly have gone wrong,’ said Arteta. ‘But the reality probably is that unfortunately we don’t know.’.

Industry observers note that saka, to return to horse racing, has the form in the book, but that is the concern. There is, perhaps, too much form at too young an age, especially when coupled with a game reliant on acceleration and intensity.

Industry observers note that rogers himself still has a lot to prove, not least because of his £117million transfer from Aston Villa to Chelsea in the summer. With that, though, he has grown. That much was evident by him taking centre stage against Croatia on Thursday night despite the presence of Harry Kane and Jude Bellingham. Previously, you suspected Rogers was waiting for the leading men to hand him his script.

Sources indicate that his tendency to come infield will suit Tuchel, too. Kane the quarterback, as we saw at Wembley, leaves a space to populate and exploit. Rogers had more touches in the penalty area than any other player, including the one for his opening goal. And if Anthony Gordon, on the opposite flank, is the one with chalk on his boots, Rogers muddying his in the goalmouth is what the team needs.

Meanwhile, Rogers has hit top gear at Chelsea and become a key man under Thomas Tuchel.

It has been revealed that this debate, Saka versus Rogers, is not one that should keep Tuchel awake at night. It is a nice problem to have - the hope that Saka will return to his best, the expectation that Rogers is still to realise his.

On Sunday, at the Metropolitano Stadium in Madrid, Rogers has another opportunity to further his claims. He has come a long way since a drab Wednesday night at Peterborough’s London Road in 2021. It is, though, the distance yet travelled that is most exciting.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Il centrocampista parla del buon avvio di stagione e del clima nel gruppo.

Fisayo Dele-Bashiru è stato intervistato ai microfoni di Lazio Style Channel al rientro dagli impegni con la Nazionale, in vista della sfida di sabato tra Lazio e Lecce. Nel confronto racconta l'energia portata da Gattuso, la concorrenza interna e la voglia di dare il massimo per la squadra.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

Sto bene. Sono felice di essere tornato a Roma. Naturalmente, essere convocato in Nazionale è sempre un momento speciale, soprattutto in occasione delle qualificazioni alla Coppa d'Africa. Le partite sono andate abbastanza bene. La prima è stata positiva, la seconda poteva andare meglio, ma sono felice di essere tornato a Roma. Nel fine settimana ci aspetta una partita importante e non vediamo l'ora di giocarla.

According to recent reports, penso che quest'anno abbiamo iniziato molto bene con Gattuso. Ha portato nuova energia nello spogliatoio e credo che questo si veda nei rapporti tra i compagni, nel nostro rapporto con l'allenatore e anche in quello con i tifosi. Se riusciremo a continuare su questa strada, sarà perfetto.

Tanto, in questo momento c'è molta concorrenza. Quando ho l'opportunità di entrare in campo per aiutare la squadra, cerco sempre di dare il massimo. Se dovessi giocare nel fine settimana, darò come sempre tutto me stesso. Credo che questo sia importante perché, per arrivare lontano in campionato, non bisogna poter contare soltanto sugli undici titolari: anche i giocatori in panchina devono dare il proprio contributo. È fondamentale.

In a recent development, credo che la concorrenza sia sicuramente positiva e faccia bene. Tutte le migliori squadre del mondo hanno molta competizione interna e penso che questo permetta alla squadra di esprimere al meglio. In questo momento l'atmosfera è molto buona. Credo che nello spogliatoio ci siano molte più battute e momenti di leggerezza rispetto alla scorsa stagione, quando la situazione era differente. Quest'anno siamo molto più uniti e questo contribuisce sicuramente a creare un bel clima all'interno del gruppo.

In a recent development, da quando sono alla Lazio ho avuto diversi allenatori. Credo che quest'anno un aspetto importante sia il grande coinvolgimento di Gattuso nel lavoro con il gruppo e con ogni singolo giocatore. Ha un ottimo rapporto con tutti i componenti della squadra e penso che questo sia fondamentale. Inoltre, sa perfettamente cosa significhi essere in campo ai massimi livelli, avendo avuto una grande carriera da calciatore. È un allenatore di altissimo livello, tutti i ragazzi gli vogliono bene e dobbiamo continuare a ottenere risultati per lui.

A livello personale sono una persona piuttosto tranquilla. Non lascio che quello che succede all'esterno influenzi troppo il mio modo di essere. Penso di comportarmi in campo proprio come nella vita di tutti i giorni: sono abbastanza rilassato e calmo, anche se so essere aggressivo quando serve. Direi che queste sono le caratteristiche che mi descrivono meglio.

A livello personale, il mio obiettivo è giocare il maggior numero possibile di partite e aiutare la squadra il più possibile, magari con gol e assist. Se riuscirò a fare tutto questo, penso che sarà una stagione davvero molto positiva, non soltanto per me, ma anche per tutti i ragazzi. Adesso dobbiamo semplicemente continuare a lavorare partita dopo partita. Speriamo di riuscire a proseguire su questa buona strada.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was Manchester United’s first foray back into the Champions League for 1,003 days, but even with hazy memories of the competition, they know full well they are unlikely to have it this easy again in Europe this season.

After an unconvincing beginning to their Premier League campaign and with Manchester City the visitors to Old Trafford on Sunday, Michael Carrick will have been grateful for a gentle start to life back among Europe’s elite.

Sources indicate that little-known Sabah of Azerbaijan have quite the story to tell, but the closest they got to making this an awkward evening for United came in the first half when, already trailing 1-0, Joy-Lance Mickels miscued an inviting header from close range. Otherwise, it was one-way traffic.

According to recent reports, united’s biggest threat on the night was complacency, but there was none of that. This was a professional, unfussy display with a few nice flourishes. Kobbie Mainoo impressed again in central midfield and Carrick was able to substitute a number of his best players early with the derby in mind, as well as resting Luke Shaw entirely.

Goals from Matheus Cunha, Bruno Fernandes and Benjamin Sesko in the first half killed the game as a contest before Lisandro Martínez scored a fourth with just over 20 minutes remaining.

Matheus Cunha opens the scoring for Manchester United with his first ever Champions League goal 🏄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/ZDQBbEfizq.

Industry observers note that “It’s nice to keep a clean sheet and obviously win the game,” Carrick stated. “Some of the football we played was really good – dangerous on the transition. The result looks comfortable, but it wasn’t always like that but we did a lot of good things.

United probably could not have asked for a softer return to Champions League football. Atlético Madrid at the Wanda Metropolitano next month will certainly be a very different beast, but it was a rewarding first 45 minutes all the same that paved the way for Carrick to ring the changes ahead of the derby.

Already leading 1-0, two goals shortly before the interval changed the complexion of the game and effectively extinguished any flickering hopes Sabah had of a gargantuan upset.

Founded just nine years ago, Sabah had navigated four qualifying rounds that began on July 7 just to reach this stage.

Throw in the fact Valdas Dambrauskas, their Lithuanian manager, got his break in coaching with the Manchester United Soccer Schools 20 years ago, and it is quite the heartwarming tale.

But there is not much sentiment at this level and, given time and space, United punished their inexperience and carelessness.

In a recent development, carrick will not read too much into the performance. City will be an entirely different proposition and it will be interesting to see whether he goes for a two-man midfield with Bruno Fernandes deployed as an advanced No 10, or perhaps operates with a midfield three and adjusts his attack.

Either way, Mainoo will be central to the game proposal.

It is hard to believe the England midfielder missed most of pre-season after reporting back late following the World Cup, because he has barely missed a beat in his last three outings, even if his team-mates have not always hummed to his tune.

There is so much to like about Mainoo. His manipulation of space, how he never looks under duress, even when hounded, and his vision on the ball. There was one lovely angled ball over the top here, after United had worked the space well, that released Fernandes in behind. His cross was cut out before Sesko could tap in.

In a recent development, mainoo’s work off the ball has improved enormously, too. There were numerous instances here of him making a timely intervention or nicking the ball away at the right moment to recover possession.United have spent £155m reconfiguring their midfield, but Mainoo will be a constant. “He’s a fantastic player, it’s pretty obvious to see,” Carrick remarked. “He has a massive influence on our games. He is a real joy to have, he wants to improve, he wants to listen and it’s great to see.”.

Kobbie Mainoo completed 81/83 passes, 6/6 accurate long balls and 10 passes into final third on his full Champions League debut ⭐️ pic.twitter.com/NK9BIGvc4m.

It will certainly be interesting to see how Carrick’s new-look midfield shapes up against City’s own revamped one in the form of Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernández and Ayyoub Bouaddi.

“There are some good connections and we have played some good football through the middle of the pitch,” Carrick added. “A lot of it is on wavelength and understanding of where each other wants the ball. We haven’t had the perfect start but there are really good signs.”.

Carrick was suitably confident to withdraw Youri Tielemans at half-time and bring on Mason Mount, who was having a good pre-season before his familiar injury jinx hit, and he will have been pleased to see Sesko on the scoresheet again. “He definitely offers a different kind of threat,” Carrick noted. “There are not many who can give us what Ben does with his physicality, playing on the last line. It’s great to have him back.”.

Sources indicate that sesko’s goal, rounding the goalkeeper to slot home from Bryan Mbeumo’s pass after line-breaking balls from Mainoo and Fernandes, capped off a quick-fire three minutes when Sabah were unpicked. Before then, Cunha had picked out Tielemans’s burst into the penalty area, from where he pulled the ball back for Fernandes to coolly finish.

Benjamin Šeško rounds the goalkeeper to make it three for Manchester United 🔄📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/tnslugsmZM.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00.

United had taken the lead when Kaheem Parris paid the price for a misplaced pass straight to Mbeumo, from which the ball was moved at pace between Sesko, Fernandes and Patrick Dorgu to tee up Cunha to score.

Industry observers note that dorgu was starting here at left-back with Shaw rested with one eye on City. It was an early glimpse of how Carrick is going to have to manage the minutes of his only recognised senior left-back, who is not going to be able to play every few days.

Carrick prefers Dorgu further up the pitch and it remains to be seen if he trusts the Dane at left-back in bigger games than this.

Industry observers note that with City having played in Porto on Tuesday and had a little extra rest time, the United manager will have been pleased he got the chance to withdraw several key players early. He was even able to give a rare run-out to Joshua Zirkzee and it was the Dutchman who helped to force the fourth goal.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q.

Fernandes’s quick free-kick caught out Sabah and Zirkzee back-heeled the ball goalwards. It bounced off Aden McCarthy and from there goalkeeper Stas Pokatilov got himself in a dreadful spin, unable to locate the ball by which point Martínez had blasted it in from a yard out.

Job done. Now a much bigger test awaits.

Industry observers note that “Nice to have a clean sheet and obviously win the game. Some of our attacking play was fantastic. We were dangerous in transition, defended well in the most part. The result looks comfortable but it was not as easy as that. Kobbie [Mainoo] is a fantastic player, it is pretty obvious to see. He has a massive influence on our game and a real joy to have. Through the middle of the pitch, we have played some good football at times and we can get better. There are some good signs which we have shown tonight. The confidence is there, like at Everton on Sunday for large spells, just took a hit there at the end with the result. It is always nice to win. Another massive one on Sunday.”.

The final whistle is blown at Old Trafford and Manchester United claim a 4-0 victory on their return to the Champions League. Goals from Cunha, Fernandes, Sesko and Martinez give Michael Carrick’s side three points in their opening game of the competition. Debutants Sabah return home with nothing and no goals, despite some decent chances to get a goal.

A number of empty seats at Old Trafford are becoming visible as some home fans have seen enough, knowing their side is going to win.

Sabah have had a few chances to come away from their Champions League debut with a goal but have wasted some great chances, including one just now. Mickels delivers a lovely cross from the left, which perfectly picks out Mbina, but his header goes just over the bar.

There will be three added minutes.

Mickels wasted a glorious chance in the first half and he comes close to goal a now but drags his shot just wide of the far post from the left side of the box.

Sources indicate that how on earth have the officials missed that one? Cunha catches Almeida on the leg and it should be at least a booking but the officials do not see it, despite the linesman being not far away. Cunha is very lucky as that was a nasty challenge.

Sabah would love to at the very least send their travelling fans back to Azerbaijan with a goal on their Champions League debut. You do wonder how different the game could have been had Mickels not missed a sitter that would have seen Sabah make it 1-1.

Michael Carrick is going to make his final two changes of the night as youngsters Lacey and Amass come on.

A bit of a soft goal for Sabah to concede. Fernandes clips in a free-kick into the Sabah box which picks out the run of Zirkzee. The Dutchman’s backheel is blocked and Sabah should then deal with the danger. However, Sabah make an absolute mess of things and their keeper Pokatilov has no idea where the ball is, allowing Martinez to nick in and smash the ball into the net.

Lisandro Martínez pounces on a defensive mistake from Sabah to make it four 🫣📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/eTAYgMmV9Q.

Lepinjica is the first Sabah player into the book tonight for a cynical trip on Mount.

Zirkzee, only just on the pitch, shoots from range but it is straight down the throat of Pokatilov.

Puchacz takes the free-kick from just over 25 yards out and strikes it well but the effort is just off target.

According to recent reports, perhaps with the Manchester derby on Sunday in mind, Michael Carrick is going to make a double change. Zirkzee and Santos replace Sesko and Mainoo.

It has been revealed that dorgu is the first player into the book tonight. Lepinjica spots the run of Parris into the right channel and plays a clever pas forward. Dorgu cynically brings Parris down and is rightly booked.

The visitors are making a change as Parris is replaced by Isaev.

Manchester United come close to a fourth and Cunha his second. The home side work it well near the Sabah penalty area with a couple of clever flicks and passes before Cunha has an effort saved by Pokatilov to his left.

Mazraoui receives it out in space on the right and cuts inside onto his left. He comes across the face of the penalty area before getting his shot away but his effort is off target.

Sabah are enjoying a decent spell of possession but have not yet threatened Lammens’ goal in this second half.

Industry observers note that is Yoro lucky? Mickels appeared to turn him not far outside the Manchester United penalty area but Yoro is not penalised. It did on first viewing look like a foul and would have been at least a yellow card.

Sources indicate that we are back under way at Old Trafford. How quickly might Michael Carrick make changes with Sunday’s Manchester derby in mind? Well, he has made one change at the break as Mount replaces Tielemans. It is Mount’s first appearance of the season. Sabah have brought on Mbina at the break.

Sources indicate that those two goals late in the half completely change the complexion of the game and Michael Carrick’s half-time team talk. Good first 45 minutes back in the Champions League for United.

Industry observers note that the first half is brought to an end and Manchester United are cruising towards victory on their return to the Champions League. It has all gone wrong for Sabah.

Recent findings suggest that that is game, set and match before half-time at Old Trafford as the dam has burst for Sabah. Sesko is played in behind by Mbeumo and is one-on-one with Pokatilov. Sesko takes it around Pokatilov before putting it into the empty net.

Sources indicate that michael Carrick’s side have their second of the night not long before half-time and it is a well-taken goal. Cunha, from the left side of the box, plays it inside to Tielemans. The Belgian takes one touch before, on the turn, playing it back into the path of Fernandes, who finds the net with a first-time finish.

Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans combine to double Manchester United's lead ✌️📺 Watch live on TNT Sports & HBO Max pic.twitter.com/nZnkwLWJ00.

Fernandes has an effort from the edge of the Sabah box but blazes his effort high over the bar.

Industry observers note that that’s a warning there for United. Fernandes gives the ball away in the middle with a heavy touch and Sabah break through the tall, languid figure of Lepinjica. Parris’ cross loops the far post where Mickels should have done better than steer an inviting header into the side netting. Bit of a let off for Carrick’s side.

Sabah should be level as they miss a sitter. Parris, from the right side of the box, clips a cross to the back post that picks out Mickels. He should score but puts his header into the side netting. That should have been the equaliser for Sabah.

Dorgu clips in a cross from the left side of the box and picks out Sesko, whose hooked first-time effort goes just wide.

Parris’ shot from the edge of the box takes a deflection and goes behind for a corner. It is wasted though by Sabah as the inswinger is easily caught by Lammens.

According to recent reports, manchester United make their return to the Champions League as they host tournament debutants Sabah of Azerbaijan on matchday one at Old Trafford. It will be the first time that Manchester United have faced an Azerbaijani side in European competition.

Recent findings suggest that manchester United have one win, one loss and one draw to their name in their opening three Premier League games. They were seconds away from winning their second game of the season on Sunday but conceded a late equaliser at Everton. They last featured in the Champions League during the 2023/24 season, when they were eliminated in the group stage, and have won just one of their last nine games in the competition.

According to recent reports, “It means an awful lot [to be back in the Champions League],” Manchester United boss Michael Carrick stated. “Challenging yourself against the elite, the very best. This football club has been used to being the best. It is not something you can take for granted. We missed out on it for a number of years and now we are back. It is where we expect to be without getting ahead of ourselves. We have made huge steps to make it in, now it is about pushing into the next chapter and evolution if the squad and this is certainly where we want to be.

Industry observers note that “I do not think it is a case of if we get to a certain stage it is a success and if we do not it is not. We have to embrace the new challenge that we are facing as a group and push to what we can push to. If we get further down the line in this competition then who knows? I am not writing anything off. But we are taking it step by step and we certainly are not getting ahead of ourselves. We have got a squad that is strong enough to compete.”.

Sabah make their Champions League debut having been founded just eight years ago in September 2017. Back in April, they secured the Azerbaijan top-flight title for the first time in their history and also won the Azerbaijan Cup in May. They earned a spot in the Champions League group stages after beating Hapoel Be’er Sheva 6-4 on aggregate. In the previous three seasons, they have tried to reach the group stages of the Europa and Conference Leagues but failed to do so. They have won all three leagues thus far, including a 5-0 home win over Zira last Saturday.

Tech Report: Former Rangers striker Peter van Vossen on THAT Old Firm miss 30 years ago today... 'I wasn't paying attention and the ball hit my shin, but I still blame Jorg Albertz!'

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2183 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 09:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:44 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • In a career spanning almost 20 years, Peter van Vossen won the Champions League, made it to the quarter-finals of the World Cup with his country and won league titles in both the Netherlands and Scotland.
  • Sources indicate that point being, it’s reductive to define his time in football by one excruciating miss.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 09:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 09:44 EST, 14 November 2026.

In a career spanning almost 20 years, Peter van Vossen won the Champions League, made it to the quarter-finals of the World Cup with his country and won league titles in both the Netherlands and Scotland.

Sources indicate that point being, it’s reductive to define his time in football by one excruciating miss. But here we are.

It’s 30 years to the day since Van Vossen missed an open goal for Rangers during a crucial Old Firm clash at Celtic Park. Leading 1-0 and with less than seven minutes remaining, the Dutch forward had a chance to seal all three points for the nine-in-a-row-chasing Light Blues. Instead, he blazed over with the goal at his mercy.

In the decades since, the spurned chance has become the benchmark by which all other misses have been measured. ‘Sure, it was bad — but was it “Van Vossen” bad?’.

Sources indicate that the man himself has seldom spoken about the events of that powder keg of a night. Until now. Living the quiet life in rural Holland, Van Vossen has given Daily Mail Sport a full account of his professional nadir.

‘I mostly remember being mad at Jorg [Albertz],’ he says. ‘I was seriously p***** off with him. Paul Gascoigne played a pass inside to me and I clipped a first-time ball in behind the Celtic defence, who were pressing high. If Jorg had just left it, I was one-on-one with the goalie and I would have fancied my chances.

Rangers striker Peter van Vossen sends the ball skywards in a crucial Old Firm clash in 1996.

‘I also thought there was a chance he might have been offside, so when you see me running through and stretching out my arms, that’s not me telling him that we’re through; that’s me telling him to leave it and get out of the way!

Sources indicate that ‘Anyway, he didn’t, I continued my run, he passed it to me and, because I was still livid when the ball arrived at me, I wasn’t paying enough attention. It took a bit of a bobble, I ended up basically hitting it with my shin and, yeah, it unfortunately flew over the bar.’.

To his relief, Rangers held on for a 1-0 win to leapfrog their bitter rivals at the top of the table, albeit only after Andy Goram saved a Pierre van Hooijdonk penalty awarded moments after Van Vossen’s horror miss.

‘Walter Smith came up to me in the dressing room afterwards and said, “It’s just as well The Goalie saved that penalty otherwise I’d have f****** killed you!”’ smiles Van Vossen.

‘It was horrible but I can laugh about it now because we won the game. I wish I had scored but I didn’t, so there’s nothing I can do except try to find the humour in it.’.

Van Vossen signed for Rangers in January 1996 in a swap deal that saw Oleg Salenko join Istanbulspor. He came with some pedigree, too, having won the Champions League with Ajax in 1995, a year after featuring for the Netherlands on their run to the last eight of the World Cup in the US.

In a recent development, at that time, Rangers, bankrolled by David Murray, were in the throes of a project designed to deliver European glory, while maintaining their dominance of Scottish football. Those two objectives, notes Van Vossen, were misaligned.

Recent findings suggest that ‘We had a quality group of players that was far better than anything else in Scotland at the time,’ he says. ‘That made us incredibly difficult to beat in the league. But when we went into European games, we were exposed. The lack of competition in the league along with the lifestyles of some of our players was not compatible with taking on champions from other countries.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I always felt like we were technically a little behind. Our training usually consisted of a warm-up, a game of football, and a warm-down. That was a big adjustment for me. At Ajax, we played in a system and we worked hard on making sure everybody knew their role. In Scotland, it seemed like there was no real system. You could run anywhere you wanted. I don’t really think I learned anything in my time there.’.

According to recent reports, that’s not to say he didn’t enjoy his two-and-a-half years in Glasgow. Quite the opposite.

‘I loved playing for Rangers,’ he states. ‘Particularly that second season [1996/97]. I started really well and scored seven or eight goals in the first handful of games. I remember people being quite surprised because I had taken some time to settle. They would joke, “Who are you, Van Vossen’s better twin brother?” But I loved it.’.

A dejected Van Vossen can't believe he's missed in a moment that would follow him forever.

He reserves particular affection for Walter Smith. ‘He was a fantastic manager and a true gentleman,’ he nods. ‘He helped me through a difficult time in my personal life. When I wasn’t in his team on the weekend, for example, I would ask him if I could go back to the Netherlands to see my children. He always noted yes on the condition that I was back in time for training at 10am on Monday.

‘He genuinely cared about his players. I remember Vitesse being interested in bringing me back to Holland and their coach Leo Beenhakker coming to watch me at Ibrox.

‘After the game, he found Walter and stated, “We want to sign Peter, but we think £300,000 is too much”. Walter said to him, “Listen to me carefully. We don’t do business like this. First, you and I will go for a lunch, have a respectful chat and only when we’ve got to know each other, that’s when we’ll talk about money”.

‘Walter came to me afterwards and said, “Look, I know you’re not playing as much as you would like but I won’t let you sign for him. This isn’t a good manager and I can’t allow it. You’re one of my players and I care about getting you the right move, not just any move”. I really respected that.’.

Van Vossen endured a much more difficult relationship with Smith’s assistant Archie Knox, a man he describes as ‘manipulative’.

‘I didn’t get on with him,’ he claims. ‘People talk a lot nowadays about creating a safe space and the right culture in workplaces. To me, Archie didn’t do that. He was always shouting, always right on top of you, in your face, kicking bottles. He behaved like a madman.

Van Vossen scored nine goals in 31 caps for the Netherlands between 1992 and 2000.

‘At Ajax, the coaches wanted to know how you were feeling. They understood that being well mentally was as key as being physically fit. Archie wasn’t interested in that. He was always aggressive, but only with the players he didn’t like. He had his favourites. If you weren’t one of them, he made sure you knew all about it.’.

Background tensions aside, Van Vossen’s first full season at Ibrox, 1996/97, has assumed a special place in Rangers’ folklore. They finished five points clear of Celtic to equal their rivals’ record of nine consecutive league titles, having laid the foundations with four league wins out of four over Tommy Burns’ side.

Despite his famous miss being the closest he ever came to scoring in an Old Firm clash, Van Vossen insists he relished those occasions.

In a recent development, ‘I loved those games,’ he says. ‘The atmosphere, home and away, was unbelievable and the quality of the players on the pitch was outstanding. To be honest, there wasn’t a whole lot of football played. There were lots of mistakes, fights and loads of running. I remember feeling tired after just ten minutes. I wasn’t built for that kind of pace! But they were great to be part of.

‘The week of Old Firm matches, you could feel the pressure building. I remember being in Glasgow city centre one day and I needed a taxi. I waved one down but when it pulled up, the driver must have been a Celtic fan because he raised his middle finger and swore at me before driving away. Whereas, with Rangers taxi drivers, it was the opposite. I honestly think they would have driven me around Scotland for free.

Van Vossen had a spell in charge of Fortuna Sittard but now labels himself a 'house husband'.

Industry observers note that ‘That’s just what football is like in Glasgow. It’s on a whole other level to anything else. I’ve played in significant derbies in the Netherlands and Turkey. Believe me, nothing comes close to the Old Firm.’.

According to recent reports, after finding his playing time limited as Rangers pursued ten-in-a-row, Van Vossen was relieved to learn that his old international manager, Dick Advocaat, would take over from Smith in time for the 1998/99 season. His joy, however, was short-lived when Murray used him as a makeweight in a transfer for Feyenoord midfielder Giovanni van Bronckhorst.

‘David Murray was a brilliant guy, but he made a huge mistake when he tried to sell me to Feyenoord behind the back of Dick Advocaat,’ states Van Vossen. ‘Dick was taking over and he was keen for me to be part of his prepares.

‘I remember he was flying from Amsterdam to Glasgow when he phoned me to talk about some of his ideas. I said, “Dick, I’m sorry, but I think I’m joining Feyenoord. The deal is almost done”. He told me to stay put and said that when he got to Glasgow, he and I were going to go and see Murray.

It has been revealed that ‘I remember Dick said to him, “How can you sell players behind my back? I need to be involved in these conversations”. Murray said, “You’re absolutely right, I apologise”. He handed me a blank cheque and said, “Peter, write down whatever number you want to stay. It’s not a problem”.

Industry observers note that ‘But I couldn’t do it. I respected him for apologising to Dick, but I had lost confidence in him. I couldn’t play for somebody who would do something like that.

Van Vossen scored 11 goals in his 36 appearances for Rangers between 1996 and 1998.

‘I took a 60 per cent drop in wages to join Feyenoord but they were the team I had supported as a boy and I needed to be somewhere I was wanted and where I was being treated with respect.’.

Although his spell at Ibrox ended on a slightly sour note, Van Vossen recalls it fondly. ‘It was a family,’ he states. ‘Everybody had a part to play, from the players on the pitch to the ladies in the kitchen. I mean, they were incredible. I remember being on a ferry one time and I got chatting to a truck driver who told me he sold flowers. We had a good conversation and exchanged numbers.

It has been revealed that ‘When I got back to Glasgow, I got in touch with him and remarked, “Can you do me a favour? Can you deliver ten bouquets of flowers to Ibrox?” Sure enough, this huge truck pulled up outside the ground one day, with something like ten thousand flowers in the back. They pulled out ten bouquets and delivered them to the ladies in the kitchen. They were delighted, but it was the least I could do. They treated you like one of their own. Like I say, we were one significant family.’.

These days, the head of that family is one of Van Vossen’s old teammates, Derek McInnes, and he’s backing him to deliver silverware.

Despite carving out a successful career, Van Vossen is remembered primarily for THAT miss.

Industry observers note that ‘I remember Derek well,’ he indicates. ‘Like me, he didn’t play every game, but he always gave 100 per cent and I expect he’ll be the same as a manager. He’s a people person and I imagine he is a fantastic man-manager. I have no doubt he’ll do a great job.’.

Having dabbled in management and punditry since hanging up his boots, Van Vossen now describes himself as a ‘house husband’ who dotes on wife Jojanneke and his stepchildren Sem, Lilly, Madée and Eva. He’s also presently writing his autobiography. The simple pleasures, he insists, are what matter most to him.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I don’t need to have lots of expensive things and a certain kind of lifestyle to be a rich man,’ he adds. ‘I’m a rich man because of the memories I have and the good times I enjoyed as a footballer.

Recent findings suggest that ‘If I close my eyes, I can still remember what it was like to run onto the pitch at Ibrox in front of 50,000 supporters, and it gives me goosebumps. I am very fortunate to have had that opportunity.’.

Il centrocampista classe 2011 è stato impiegato da Rughetti in tutte le partite della stagione.

It has been revealed that andrea Morresi è il regista del centrocampo della Lazio di Rughetti. Secondo quanto riportato da Gazzetta Regionale, Il classe 2011, arrivato dal Perugia nell’estate del 2025, gioca davanti alla difesa ed è stato impiegato dal tecnico in tutte le partite di questa stagione. Nel derby con la Roma, un suo filtrante ha messo Coppola nelle condizioni di segnare il gol del momentaneo 2-1.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

It has been revealed that morresi era approdato nella capitale nella passata stagione, entrando nell’Under 15. Si è preso presto le chiavi della mediana biancoceleste, interpretando il ruolo di playmaker anche nel campionato attuale. La sua presenza è un punto fermo nelle scelte di Rughetti.

According to recent reports, prima del passaggio al Perugia, Morresi è cresciuto nel settore giovanile della Treiese, dai Piccoli Amici ai Pulcini. L’arrivo alla Lazio nell’estate del 2025 ha aperto una nuova tappa del suo percorso: con la maglia biancoceleste ha trovato spazio stabilmente davanti alla difesa.

It has been revealed that in quella posizione gestisce il pallone, distribuisce il gioco e cerca gli spazi per i compagni. Alla visione di gioco unisce tecnica e corsa nelle due fasi. Il suo destro si è già fatto notare anche sui calci di punizione, una soluzione con cui può rendersi decisivo.

Industry observers note that il suo contributo non si esaurisce però nella regia arretrata. Quando si apre la possibilità, Morresi avanza verso la trequarti avversaria. È dunque coinvolto sia nella costruzione delle azioni sia nel lavoro che precede le iniziative offensive della squadra.

Sources indicate that fino alla domenica del derby, la Lazio condivideva con la Roma l’imbattibilità in campionato. I biancocelesti si presentavano alla sfida con una struttura difensiva che li rendeva la seconda miglior difesa del raggruppamento. Anche il lavoro di Morresi davanti alla retroguardia contribuisce all’equilibrio della squadra.

Contro i giallorossi, il numero 4 ha giocato in una zona di campo particolarmente affollata. Dall’altra parte c’era il miglior attacco del girone, capace di mettere alla prova la mediana biancoceleste. La Roma ha prevalso per 3-1 dopo aver dominato gran parte degli 80 minuti, ma nella ripresa la Lazio ha trovato la forza di reagire.

L’episodio che ha riaperto momentaneamente la partita è nato dai piedi di Morresi. Un suo passaggio filtrante ha raggiunto Coppola in posizione favorevole; il compagno ha poi mandato il pallone in rete per il 2-1. La speranza biancoceleste si è spenta con il terzo gol romanista, firmato da Abate.

Il mercato di gennaio resta incerto: Lotito cerca il via libera e Fabiani valuta anche il centrocampista apprezzato da Gattuso.

Marco Brescianini e Denis Man sono due profili sondati da Fabiani per la Lazio, mentre resta da chiarire se il club potrà operare nel mercato di gennaio. Secondo quanto riportato da Lottomatica, Lotito sta lavorando a un piano economico-finanziario che permetta al direttore sportivo di cercare rinforzi per Gattuso, secondo quanto riferisce Lottomatica.

CLICCA QUI E SEGUI LAZIOPRESS.IT ANCHE SU INSTAGRAM.

In a recent development, fino a qualche settimana fa, il blocco del mercato sembrava quasi certo. Lotito punta però a ottenere il via libera della Commissione indipendente, che ha preso il posto della Covisoc.

Tra le operazioni su cui lavora ci sono l’anticipo dei crediti futuri legati alle sponsorizzazioni e una proroga per dilazionare il pagamento delle vecchie imposte relative agli anni del Covid. Dall’esito di questo lavoro dipende la possibilità per Fabiani di intervenire a gennaio.

Recent findings suggest that nel frattempo, Fabiani sta valutando diversi calciatori. Uno dei nomi indicati è Marco Brescianini, che la fonte presenta come giocatore di proprietà della Fiorentina. Gattuso lo apprezza soprattutto per la capacità di inserirsi in area di rigore.

L’operazione non viene considerata semplice. La Lazio può comunque contare su un elemento nei rapporti per un’eventuale trattativa: Brescianini ha lo stesso agente di Pinamonti.

The four problems Mauricio Pochettino needs to fix at Man United: From big names causing unrest in the dressing room to an problem which plagued Ruben Amorim and Michael Carrick before him, these are the items top of his Old Trafford in-tray

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 7 min read (1363 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 10:51 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Mauricio Pochettino will see out his final two games as US national team boss with a double-header against Haiti before starting work at Manchester United on Wednesday.
  • The 54-year-old won’t have any time to waste with a daunting first game against United’s bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday followed by a European clash with Sporting Lisbon in Portugal three days later.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CHRIS WHEELER, NORTHERN SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 21:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 10:51 EST, 14 November 2026.

Mauricio Pochettino will see out his final two games as US national team boss with a double-header against Haiti before starting work at Manchester United on Wednesday.

The 54-year-old won’t have any time to waste with a daunting first game against United’s bitter rivals Liverpool at Anfield a week on Sunday followed by a European clash with Sporting Lisbon in Portugal three days later.

With United languishing in the Premier League relegation zone and 17th in the Champions League standings, it’s clear why Pochettino has been brought in to replace Michael Carrick on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

Daily Mail Sport looks at the most pressing matters in Pochettino’s in-tray at Carrington as the former Tottenham, Chelsea and Paris Saint-Germain boss and his backroom staff head for Manchester...

Mauricio Pochettino is the newly introduced manager of Manchester United - but the problems he has to fix are already piling up.

It sounds obvious, but winning games to get United out of the Premier League drop zone has to be the first priority.

Everything at a football club flows from the results on the pitch, and United’s humiliating decline this season has had ramifications throughout Old Trafford and Carrington.

The players are clearly low on confidence which has only exacerbated the team’s dismal performances and brought just one win in 10 Premier League games, against newly-promoted Ipswich – United’s worst start in 40 years.

Diogo Dalot is a prime example, after fans cheered his substitution in the 4-4 draw against Aston Villa last weekend, and the defender cut a crestfallen figure as he left Old Trafford to go on international duty with Portugal.

The Stretford End also turned on the players as the atmosphere turned toxic after the 3-0 home defeat by Bournemouth at the end of last month, having vented their anger towards the club’s ownership – the Glazer family and Sir Jim Ratcliffe – as well as chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox at every opportunity.

That won’t go away anytime soon, but a winning team will at least take some of the sting out of the situation if appointing Pochettino can give United a ‘bounce’ and divert attention back onto the pitch.

United players are low on confidence, not least Diogo Dalot (left) whose substitution was cheered by his own fans against Aston Villa.

The United team were also lambasted by the Stretford End after the 3-0 loss to Bournemouth last month.

Carrick enjoyed a good start, losing just two of his 17 games in charge in the second half of last season to earn a two-year contract, but United struggled under him this term due to a combination of poor recruitment, injuries and lack of fitness.

Industry observers note that these are all complications that Pochettino must try to put right. There is little he can do about recruitment until the January transfer window opens and United have a chance to atone for their mistake in not signing cover at left back and centre forward last summer, which backfired spectacularly when both Luke Shaw and Benjamin Sesko picked up injuries.

He can, however, try to get more out of United’s £155million midfield signings Carlos Baleba – once he is fit again – Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos, and a United squad that was good enough to finish third in the Premier League last season.

Injuries have been a major problem with the hamstring strain that will keep Baleba out of action for Pochettino’s first few weeks in charge just the latest setback.

As well as Shaw, Sesko, Baleba and long-term casualty Manuel Ugarte, United have also lost Amad Diallo, Marcus Rashford, Kobbie Mainoo, Lisandro Martinez, Patrick Dorgu and Noussair Mazraoui for parts of this season.

Pochettino must get more out of United’s £155million midfield signing Carlos Baleba – once he is fit again.

United have struggled to keep up with their opponents since the opening day - a lack of fitness has plagued every manager since Ole Gunnar Solskjaer.

Sources indicate that the good news for Pochettino is that Shaw and Rashford are hoping to be fit for Anfield, while Matthijs de Ligt is available again after a year out with back problems. However, Sesko’s absence until the new year leaves the new boss without his most natural source of goals.

Fitness is another matter and United have looked short of it since the opening-day defeat at Hull City amid concerns that the coaching levels dropped off under Carrick and were too relaxed.

They covered 120.8 kilometres against Villa – the most in a league game under Carrick – and Pochettino will demand that and a whole lot more as he increases the work-rate among his latest squad.

It’s a problem that has hindered a succession of United bosses going back to Ole Gunnar Solskjaer, and the Argentine must find a way to drill a better work ethic into United.

The problems at United this season have inevitably led to unrest in the dressing room, with the biggest issue centred around captain Bruno Fernandes.

News that Fernandes has rejected United’s latest contract offer has come as no surprise given his dramatic change in fortunes from last season, and Pochettino must find a way to get arguably United’s best player back in form and onside.

Having set a new Premier League record for assists and picked up a string of player of the year awards last season, Fernandes’ form has dropped off a cliff as he struggled with an injury sustained at the World Cup, and he suffered the rare indignity of being benched for the loss to Bournemouth.

Never one to hide his mood very well, the 32-year-old criticised Carrick’s tactics after the Champions League defeat by Como in what was a major blow to his head coach.

Never one to hide his mood very well, Bruno Fernandes has been disgruntled of late and rejected United's offer of a new contract.

Lisandro Martinez looks to be headed for the exit door - although the arrival of his fellow Argentine Pochettino may help things.

While the United hierarchy will try to persuade Fernandes to sign a new deal in keeping with their reduced wage structure and the fact he will turn 33 next year, Pochettino has to find a way of relighting the fire in his skipper.

According to recent reports, whether the club will make as much effort to keep Lisandro Martinez as he comes towards the end of his contract remains to be seen after another member of United’s leadership team took aim at Wilcox’s recruitment after the defeat by Atletico Madrid. It is said to have caused an angry clash between Martinez and summer signing Tielemans on the way back from Spain.

Martinez looks to be heading for the Old Trafford exit, but it will be interesting to see if the arrival of his compatriot Pochettino – a combative Argentine centre back in much the same mould as a player – has an impact on that.

Sources indicate that as a former defender, Pochettino won’t need telling that leaking 15 goals in the last five games simply isn’t good enough. United have now let in 30 in all competitions this season, the most of any club in Europe’s top five leagues apart from Lens.

They have been appalling at the back, conceding in the opening seconds to Atletico, Como and Villa. Had they been able to hold out and prevent late equalisers against Everton and Tottenham, the additional four points would have them 12th in the table rather than in the relegation zone.

A revolving door of makeshift left backs in the absence of Shaw and Dorgu, De Ligt’s belated comeback and Martinez’s needless red card at Chelsea haven’t helped.

Goalkeeper Senne Lammens, so composed last season, looks considerably more shaky behind a leaky and ever-changing back-four, and had arguably his worst game against Villa last weekend.

Pochettino couldn’t ask for a tougher first test than going to Anfield, and knows that United will have to start by being solid at the back.

Il Milan continua a cercare un rinforzo offensivo e Nicolò Tresoldi è uno dei principali obiettivi per gennaio. Il Club Brugge, tuttavia, valuta il centravanti classe 2004 almeno 60 milioni di euro. I numeri del giovane attaccante sono importanti: 8 gol e un assist in campionato, oltre a 5 reti in Champions League, compresa la tripletta contro l’Inter. Il suo tifo per i rossoneri potrebbe rappresentare un ulteriore elemento a favore dell'operazione.

According to recent reports, gerry Cardinale punta a riportare il Milan ai vertici e valuta un mercato invernale ambizioso. Per l'attacco resta forte il nome di Endrick, per il quale i rossoneri potrebbero presentare al Real Madrid un'offerta da 70 milioni tra parte fissa e bonus. Xabi Alonso hits out at ‘soft’ Chelsea players

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.
  • Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.
  • Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Xabi Alonso accused his Chelsea players of being “soft” after they failed to keep a clean sheet for the 20th successive Premier League game.

Chelsea threw away an early lead to draw 2-2 with Hull City and have conceded two or more goals in each of their four Premier League games.

Alonso has tried different systems and different players in those games, but suggested Chelsea’s biggest problem is mental.

The club’s dreadful clean-sheet record pre-dates him and is the first time in 65 years Chelsea have gone 20 league games without keeping the opposition out.

According to recent reports, hull’s first goal from Mohamed Belloumi came after the ball had bounced over Jorrel Hato and Alonso said: “We need to be aware that from any situation, any team in the Premier League can hurt you. Today it was from a long ball, two bounces, the way it happened. You need to be very aware, very ready that the danger can come from any situation. If you are soft or if you are not prepared, you will get punished and we have been punished that way.”.

Chelsea have shared 30 goals with their opponents in the club’s six games in all competitions so far this season.

“Yeah, it’s all maybe entertaining, but I hope that one day you say it was a boring game and we win and we don’t give these entertaining moments,” he noted.

In a recent development, “But, for sure, it kind of repeats some patterns that we are making. It will take time to... or it will take moments to fix them when we get the lead and you still need to be competing and not give the chance so easily for them to come back, especially in the first goal, we can do much better.

“It was too soft to give them this hope because until then we were controlling, we were creating chances. But that momentum that we had changed the mood and the score of the game, and it’s something that we need to be talking [about], we address and we will get better. But it’s having an impact on our performances at the moment.”.

It has been revealed that asked if his players have a real desire to defend and keep clean sheets, Alonso said: “We can do better, we can do better for sure. We need to know that even when we have the lead, a very important part of the game is to hold together, to keep the distance, to go intense in the situations to defend. I’m sure that we can do better.

“Overall, I think that we are attacking better than defending in every part. We know that it’s a significant topic and a big theme for us. For sure, it’s just four games. But the dynamic in terms of conceding, I don’t like it and we need to do much better. Open play, set-pieces, long balls, this toughness, this competitive sense, we can do better.”.

Needing three goals or more to win games is not sustainable, as Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso is finding out.

Sources indicate that this is not a problem of Alonso’s making, given Chelsea have now gone 20 Premier League games without a clean sheet. But he is certainly not improving the problem yet.

Chelsea beat Fulham with three goals and Brighton with four but left themselves far too much to do against Arsenal and were taken advantage of by Hull City, who will be slightly disappointed they did not leave Stamford Bridge with all three points.

Goalkeeper Emiliano Martínez has now conceded seven goals in three games since joining from Aston Villa, while central defender Maxence Lacroix, who joined for £52m from Crystal Palace in the summer, was relegated to the substitutes’ bench.

Martínez was at fault for Mohamed Belloumi’s second goal, but the Argentine did make a crucial save at his back post to stop substitute Mohamed-Ali Cho grabbing a winner that Chelsea could have had no complaints about.

Hull finished the game with more shots on goal than their hosts and a higher expected-goals rate. Chelsea are far too open and in some ways far too entertaining.

Industry observers note that defensive midfielder Moisés Caicedo cannot return from injury swiftly enough, but this does not feel like a problem that will be solved by one man. Alonso needs to find a balance and instil a real desire in his team to defend.

Caicedo has that desire, but there are no defenders at the club who have shown that absolute desperation to keep the ball out of the net that Chelsea fans became so used to in the days of John Terry, Gary Cahill and César Azpilicueta.

None of this should diminish Hull’s performance. They were not only spirited and full of character but also showed quality and a threat. The joke is currently on those who laughed at their hopes of survival before a ball had been kicked.

It is now two wins and two draws for Sergej Jakirovic’s team and they are already a fifth of the way to 40 points. Jakirovic had promised his staff a week off in the international break if they reached eight points after five games. With that target already met, there may be a new reward if Hull can make it 11 points against Newcastle United next weekend.

“Before the season, I mentioned to my staff that we will take seven, eight points in these first five and then I will give them seven days off,” Jakirovic said. “That was our target and now we are in a very good position, eight points.

Industry observers note that “Especially today, it’s very, very difficult to play here, and now we will try to get even more. Of course, I’m a little bit worried about the international break because we have 13 national team players. But we will see who will come back and in what condition. So this is my concern right now.” Asked if his staff’s seven-day break will be extended if Hull can beat Newcastle, Jakirovic added: “I will tell them. But I know already.”.

Industry observers note that while his five-game target may need modifying, Jakirovic is not deviating from his goal for the season for Hull. “Our target is always to stay in the league and collect as many points as possible,” he said. “Forty points, 38 to 41, this is the average we need. Then it’s easier to play. You can play more relaxed, with more joy and happiness. So [get to] this as soon as possible, so that we are safe.”.

Industry observers note that hull had not conceded a league goal before this and there had been predictions they might crumble when they finally let the ball into their net. They did so after just seven minutes but they kept their heads and came back stronger.

It was far too easy for Morgan Rogers to make a yard of space for himself to shoot after collecting the ball from João Pedro, and Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis may not have been happy to have been beaten at his near post.

Chelsea have now scored inside the first 10 minutes in all of their four league games, but Hull were in no mood to crumble and hit back with two goals in six minutes from Belloumi to take a half-time lead. Both Hull goals were shockers from Chelsea’s perspective. The first, in the 28th minute, came as a result of Jorrel Hato letting the ball bounce over him from a Ryan Giles cross and Belloumi finished brilliantly.

Belloumi’s second came after Martínez had flapped at a corner and Semi Ajayi had hit the bar with a header. The ball fell to Belloumi again and his shot was deflected into the net.

It was no surprise that Hato did not reappear for the second half, as he was replaced by Pep Chavarría at left-back. But Chelsea remained vulnerable and Martínez had to recover from spilling a Regan Slater shot to prevent Ollie McBurnie extending Hull’s advantage.

When Palmer and Pedro combined for Pedro to sweep the ball into the net and equalise with 24 minutes remaining, it seemed like it would be Chelsea who would provide the grandstand finish.

But it was Hull who got a second wind and Chelsea were indebted to Martínez for making a save to stop Cho securing all three points and sending the visiting fans home even happier.

I feel good. We have to be happy. It’s a huge result for us.

We had 2-1 at half-time and we had a 100 per cent chance with McBurnie but Martinez’s save was excellent. We have to control play better in the box because we can stop this [Chelsea goal]. We had an excellent chance for Cho – Martinez saved again. Player of the match.

We can be very happy. We took a point in a very demanding match.

Recent findings suggest that eight points against very difficult opponents. We have to continue like this.

Not a single home win in the Premier League, today.

According to recent reports, A sweet strike from one of Palace’s summer signings, recruited from Union Saint Gilloise, and that is his first Palace goal. The 22-year-old Israeli came through at Maccabi Haifa. Uphill task for Gary O’Neill and Ipswich.

Austin MacPhee, Chelsea’s flamboyant set-piece coach, just motioned for Xabi Alonso to sit down when the Blues manager momentarily got up from his seat when the home side were preparing to take a corner. It seems MacPhee wears the (correct length) trousers when it comes to set pieces.

According to recent reports, an almighty let off for Alisson and Liverpool after pass from the goalkeeper played Gravenberch into trouble, but Jacquet cleared off the line to keep the game goalless. That was Fulham’s first foray forward.

According to recent reports, A bright start in this game and there is no chance it will end goalless (famous last words). Andoni Iraola has made three changes from the team that beat Atletico Madrid on Wednesday and it’s a pattern of his early management that he is making the kind of decisions that supporters are nodding along in approval with. Liverpool should already be one up but Alexander Isak’s shot has just drifted across the face of goal but the signs are encouraging. It could be a long afternoon for Alvaro Arbeloa.

Wow. Unbelievable double save from Forest’s Matz Sels there to keep out Victor Lindelof.

The first was the most impressive, a reflex stop after a deflection.

Morgan Rogers is the first player to score against Hull City this season. Emi Martinez debuted the ball forward after claiming a corner, and Rogers’ shot from the edge of the area crept under the goalkeeper Tzolakis. He will not want to watch that one again.

According to recent reports, we’re past five minutes and it’s the longest Chelsea have gone without scoring in the league this season. Back on Matt Crooks – one of his middle names is Rider.

It has been revealed that although Rogers scored in the seventh minute...so the early goals continue for Chelsea. It will be difficult for Hull now.

Twelve seconds in and the chant “where were you in Istanbul” gets a very early airing from Villa’s home fans.

That is of course a reference to Villa’s 4-0 win over Forest in the Europa League semi-final second leg last season.

The early indications are that Reece James is playing in midfield with Malo Gusto at right-back in a conventional back four.

Xabi Alonso has made an encouraging start to life as Chelsea manager. But his trousers upset me. They are three inches too short and a bit baggy above the ankle.

We are under way in the five Premier League 3pm kick-offs. Goals and further updates from around the grounds as they happen.

Some early #analysis from Matt at the Bridge, about one of Hull’s midfielders.

Matt Crooks is absolutely massive.

One player who has really shone for Villa so far this season is teenage midfielder George Hemmings.

Unai Emery has been very impressed with the academy graduate, who made his Champions League debut on Tuesday night.

There is also a massive buzz around £51m signing Johan Manzambi, who is on the bench today after recovering from a knee injury.

In a recent development, will we get another fast start from Chelsea today? They have scored inside the first five minutes in all three of their League games this season. Hull are yet to concede.

Industry observers note that dominic King writes that there were signs of promise in the relationship between Barcola, Wirtz and Isak in Liverpool’s win over Atletico Madrid, and all three forwards start against Fulham. Timothy Castagne, Fulham’s right-back will need to have his sprinting boots on against Barcola, who is grease lightning.

Cole Palmer has 15 goal involvements in his 15 Premier League games for Chelsea against newly promoted sides.9 goals ⚽6 assists 🅰️ pic.twitter.com/PJIU0YxIhQ.

It has been revealed that I’m having real fun. I’ve got a smile on face and I’m enjoying my football. Playing with players like [Palmer and Joao Pedro] inspire you to be better and make you do better and do well for the team. We are in a good moment and we want to keep it going.

Hull are really tough to beat. They have played against some good opponents and they’ve kept them out - they haven’t conceded yet. It is going to be difficult because they are really organised but we are at home and it is on us to make the game about us.

Industry observers note that we know it is always tough against Brentford. We can expect a tight game today, definitely. We both want to win so it’ll be a nice game.

We are very excited about our first European game coming up but we haven’t really spoken about it lately because we have just spoken about this game. This is a major game and we are looking for our first three points of the season. We have been close in every game so we hope to get it today.

Unai Emery is possibly the best coach in the Premier League but has found past encounters with Oliver Glasner very uncomfortable.

Since Glasner’s arrival in English football with Crystal Palace in February 2024, he has faced Emery’s Villa seven times and never lost.

With five victories and two draws, it is an impressive record albeit with a different set of players.

Aston Villa and Forest are two teams in transition, and meet for the first time since that two-legged Europa League semi-final last season.

Villa are building a new chapter after a summer of significant change, while Forest are implementing a totally different style of play under Oliver Glasner.

There have been signs of progress at both of the former European Cup winners. Villa secured an impressive victory over Club Brugge in the Champions League on Tuesday. Forest are improving under Glasner, with their best performance the 2-2 draw at Liverpool.

Returning to Villa Park will have some bitter memories for a number of the Forest players, after that 4-0 defeat in the second leg of the Europa League.

The Reds to take on Fulham 🔴 #LIVFUL pic.twitter.com/PpuyPkkNxU.

Ollie Watkins and Emi Martinez departed for pastures latest in the transfer window.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of this afternoon’s Premier League three o’clock kick-offs, and home bankers would appear to be the theme of the day.

According to recent reports, liverpool will be strongly fancied to put Fulham to the sword at Anfield, with confidence low at the London club and new manager Alvaro Arbeloa (once a player at Anfield) already under pressure amid reports of dressing room unrest. Andoni Iraola secured his first Premier League victory as Liverpool manager at Ipswich last time out, and backed up that result with a come-from-behind win against Atletico Madrid in the Champions League.

In a recent development, chelsea host Hull City, who are unbeaten after three games and have yet to concede a goal. It is a remarkable start to the season for Sergej Jakirović‘s side, who continue to defy expectations as well as the underlying data. For all their spirit and defensive organisation, keeping out Cole Palmer, Morgan Rogers and Joao Pedro at Stamford Bridge promises to be a tall order, though.

Recent findings suggest that aston Villa’s rocky start to the campaign took a turn for the better with a 3-2 Champions League victory at Club Brugge, and as the weeks go by Unai Emery’s team should grow stronger as their raft of young signings bed in. Nottingham Forest could be obdurate opponents, although Villa swept them aside in the second leg of last season’s Europa League semi-final. Oliver Glasner’s Crystal Palace were a bogey team for Villa though, with the Austrian coach undefeated against Emery having notched up some resounding victories.

Industry observers note that glasner’s former club Palace could do with a home win against Ipswich Town, while there is cigarette paper between Bournemouth and Brentford, two of the league’s smartest operators who play at the Vitality Stadium this afternoon. Bournemouth qualified for Europe at Brentford’s expense last season, but Marco Rose is looking for his first league win despite some encouraging performances.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, middlesbrough are sat joint-top of the Championship table at the moment along with Birmingham City and Stoke City after 15 fixtures. They drew 0-0 away at Watford last time out before the international break.

It has been revealed that kim Hellberg‘s side are back in action this weekend as they aim to return to winning ways after two games without a win. They face Bristol City at the Riverside Stadium.

According to recent reports, ikeme, who had a loan spell at Boro from Wolves back in 2011, has delivered his verdict on his ex-club, as per The Yorkshire Post: “I think they’ll be disappointed if they don’t go up automatically this year but that being said, with Wolves, West Ham and Burnley coming down, it’s going to be tough to get up for anyone. You’ve got the teams in and around the play-off picture, you’ve got the chasing pack as well.”.

Sources indicate that he added: “Out of the teams that were left in the Championship, they do look like the strongest. I think Wolves will be hoping to kick on as the year goes on but Boro do look like one of the teams that will be in and around it.”.

According to recent reports, middlesbrough reached the play-off final in the last campaign. However, they were beaten at Wembley by Hull City.

Boro lacked a proper number nine last term and that was the main reason why they didn’t get into the top two in the end. They have solved that issue with the addition of Will Lankshear from Tottenham Hotspur and he has been prolific.

Lankshear, 21, has scored 15 goals in 16 games in all competitions since his summer switch. He has sat out of their last two matches due to injury against Wrexham and Watford respectively and his team haven’t won without.

Industry observers note that middlesbrough aren’t just a one man team though and have some eye-catching talent at their disposal. Aidan Morris, Sebastian Berhalter and Amario Cozier-Duberry, among others, will all fancy their chances of playing at the top level soon.

Middlesbrough can’t just rely on Lankshear to fire in the goals for them. They need other players like David Strelec and Kyle Joseph to step up to the plate as well.

Industry observers note that strelec has only just returned from injury and could still play a key role over the coming weeks and months. As for Joseph, he has struggled to make an impact since his switch from Hull City in the last transfer window.

Industry observers note that the ex-Blackpool man hasn’t scored in the league yet for Hellberg’s side. Boro are having to be patient with him at the moment.

Sources indicate that middlesbrough have an ideal opportunity to return to winning ways this Saturday against Bristol City as they look to get back to the summit. Their upcoming opponents have been in poor form recently and pressure is starting to mount on their head coach Michael Skubala.

#49697. Mauricio Pochettino's Man United SQUAD AUDIT: Axe EIGHT stars, new role for the attacker he's 'always liked' and who could be his new Dele Alli... now give YOUR player-by-player verdict

📅 13 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 23m • 📚 Deep Dive (4597 w)
