Mauricio Pochettino's Man United SQUAD AUDIT: Axe EIGHT stars, new role for the attacker he's 'always liked' and who could be his new Dele Alli... now give YOUR player-by-player verdict

📅 13 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4597 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:11 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Walking into a club in turmoil is nothing latest for Mauricio Pochettino.
  • Recent findings suggest that he arrived at Southampton with the Saints three points clear of the relegation zone.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By NATHAN SALT - FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 07:00 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 11:11 EST, 14 November 2026.

Walking into a club in turmoil is nothing latest for Mauricio Pochettino.

Recent findings suggest that he arrived at Southampton with the Saints three points clear of the relegation zone. Tottenham Hotspur were crying out for some leadership after Andre Villas-Boas and Tim Sherwood's spells, while Chelsea picked up Pochettino in 2023 on the back of their lowest league finish for more than 25 years.

Recent findings suggest that now it's Manchester United that require what Victor Wanyama once described as Pochettino's 'magic touch' – and they need it quick as they sit in the relegation zone with ten games played. Pochettino remains weeks removed from the January transfer window and has a number of first-team regulars out with long-term injuries, so his reputation of improving the players at his disposal will be put to the test.

He has developed a reputation for placing faith in youth – while at Tottenham, Pochettino handed 12 debuts to players aged 21 or under, more than any other manager.

Money will be tight and United look almost certain to miss out on next season's Champions League, which will make squad development significantly harder, so Pochettino will have to make do and mend with a lot of the current underperforming crop of players.

With all that in mind, Daily Mail Sport runs the rule over the 36 players Pochettino will be inheriting when he walks through the door at Carrington next week.

And you can scroll to the end of the article to have your say on who should stay, and who should go...

Mauricio Pochettino will rapidly have to assess which Man United players to discard.

Industry observers note that lammens won't be going anywhere. He is United's No 1 and despite a downturn in form this season, he's not become a bad goalkeeper overnight. Pochettino's trusted goalkeeping coach Toni Jimenez will almost certainly replace Craig Mawson to bring some fresh ideas.

In a recent development, jimenez focuses a lot on developing goalkeepers to be comfortable as sweepers and playing higher up. That is a sore spot in Lammens' game – recently exposed by Bournemouth striker Evanilson – but proper coaching should help develop Lammens, just like Jimenez developed Hugo Lloris.

A summer arrival from Leeds United as a back-up goalkeeper. Pochettino has more notable problems than messing around with his No2.

Industry observers note that heaton is hugely popular at the club and while he doesn't play, he is viewed as a vital cog in the dressing room given his wealth of experience. He turns 41 later this season and has been busy preparing for life away from the pitch.

Heaton has completed courses on becoming a sporting director, as well as an executive leadership short course from Oxford University.

He also holds his goalkeeper coach B-Licence, A-Licence outfield, and a certificate of football management from UEFA.

In a recent development, pochettino would be wise to keep Heaton in-house, even if not as a player. He is a respected figure who knows United inside out and that shouldn't be overlooked as Pochettino tries to build out a culture.

Senne Lammens (right) has made a shaky start to the season but will be going nowhere.

Dalot is highly respected by every manager that works with him for the effort he puts in, something that can't always be said of some of his team-mates.

But he is woefully short of the required quality to take United forward and he is not a comfortable fit for Pochettino's ideals, either.

Pochettino gets width in his sides via the full backs and that requires a relentless runner – which Dalot is – having quality both defensively and in attack, which Dalot does not.

Malo Gusto, who is keen to leave Chelsea and could become a key target for United, spoke of how Pochettino developed his game in 2024 when he mentioned: 'He helps us a lot. He has tried to show us the desire to win, to keep fighting against every team.

According to recent reports, 'He talks to us a lot about tactics, technique and everything. He is a good person as well. He tries to help us a lot on the pitch and off it. He is a good coach for this young team.

According to recent reports, 'He is here for this. He knows he has to wake up our mentality, to wake up our desire to win everything.'.

United have neglected their back-line for years and it's time for a dramatic refresh, starting with shifting Dalot, who is under contract until 2028.

It is time for Man United to move on from Diogo Dalot - he is short of the quality required.

Noussair Mazraoui (Full back, 28).

Dalot has at least shown he has the engine to get up and down, which could offer a lifeline under Pochettino, but Mazraoui hasn't.

Full backs are essential to Pochettino's high-intensity, high press 4-2-3-1, and that's not a formula that suits Mazraoui's abilities.

Privately, sources close to the dressing room have suggested in recent weeks that Mazraoui, another under contract until 2028, is keen for a latest challenge.

Matthijs de Ligt (centre back, 27).

Overhauling the defence is one of the main topics of conversation among agents and players right now but De Ligt's future is secure at Old Trafford.

He is under contract until 2029, with the option of a further year, and many figures behind the scenes believe he can bounce back from such a long period out with injury to be a success.

De Ligt's injury record, as well as the fact he isn't a natural fit for Pochettino's idea of the perfect, mobile centre back, makes him an intriguing prospect.

Strong in physical duels, he could become a key squad player.

Harry Maguire (centre back, 33).

Maguire has taken more criticism than most during his time at United and deserves credit for how he has overcome it.

His contract expires in the summer, with the option of a further year, and Maguire has described playing for United as the 'ultimate honour' so is unlikely to agitate to leave.

That being remarked, Pochettino puts a lot of emphasis on recovery pace given the high line he has favoured in the past and the Argentine's tactics have routinely exposed centre backs in transition, with speed essential to masking shortcomings.

Maguire would undoubtedly struggle in that department and while his physical profile would appeal, he said earlier this year that he does not want to be kept around for 'sentimental value'.

It has been revealed that 'I love this club. But it's got to be right for myself, it's got to be right for the club as well,' Maguire said in March before a one-year extension was triggered.

Recent findings suggest that 'I don't want to be staying on sentimental value. I want to be staying because I want to be there and the club want me to drive the club forward still, and they feel like I've got a big part to play in it.'.

The prospect of a diminishing role, with United planning multiple defensive reinforcements, may see both sides agree it's time for a change.

After seven years it may be time for Harry Maguire to move on, with his contract expiring.

Lisandro Martinez (centre back, 28).

A player that looks to have one foot out the door after calling out director of football Jason Wilcox following the defeat by Atletico Madrid.

It has been revealed that it's funny, almost, given Pochettino's arrival should suit Martinez down to the ground. In theory, he is the exact type of player his compatriot would implore his bosses to recruit.

Pochettino puts huge emphasis on passing out from the back and Martinez is the best in that category among United's centre backs.

Pochettino is also incredibly intense, something Martinez has been for some time at United, sometimes to the group's benefit and sometimes to its detriment.

The Argentine's contract expires in the summer and while there is an option to trigger a further year to avoid a World Cup winner walking away for nothing, the expectation is that he won't agree to a newly introduced one and his time at United is more likely than not drawing to a close.

In a recent development, he holds a desire to play in Spain and that may not vanish overnight. But if anyone can connect with Martinez about a longer-term role, it's a fellow Argentine.

VERDICT: Keep (but expect to go!).

Patrick Dorgu (Full back/winger, 22).

Has the potential to be the biggest winner of the Pochettino appointment.

Pochettino's full-back-turned-winger style totally plays into Dorgu's hands given both his engine and his comfort playing higher up the pitch. Look at the development of Danny Rose – who played more games for Pochettino than any other player – and Kyle Walker, as well as Sergino Dest with the USA.

Dorgu has a lot of the attributes Pochettino craves while he also remains raw enough that intense, but targeted, coaching could improve him.

He should immediately become one of Pochettino's go-to men.

Where there are concerns around Maguire's ability to play in a system which squeezes everyone that bit higher up the pitch, Yoro should thrive.

He revealed against Villa, with a chase down to deny Nicolas Jackson a run on goal, that he possesses the necessary recovery pace.

Pochettino's centre backs need to be strong passers and Yoro can improve in this area, although he has shown a willingness to dictate with long diagonals, as well as burst through lines as a ball-carrier.

United need five reliable centre backs in the squad moving forward and Yoro can establish himself as the No1.

Given Pochettino's track record with young players, he should be really excited at becoming a key piece of the puzzle under him.

A reunion… but one that may not last very long.

In a 2017 book about Pochettino, Shaw revealed his desire to work under him again and that wish has now come true.

'With Southampton he achieved the impossible,' mentioned Shaw. 'We were one of the best footballing teams in the league... I do hope that I can play for him again one day. And I think he really wants me to play under him again.'.

Pochettino used to call Shaw his 'son' and their relationship has stayed strong over the years.

But Pochettino is also a winner and will be acutely aware that Shaw cannot maintain the levels that Pochettino will require from his full backs after years of injury problems.

Sources close to the player have suggested the potential for a one-year extension given the relationship with Pochettino, even if those same sources believe the time is right for a fresh start.

A long servant but not one that can take United forward from this lowest of ebbs.

Luke Shaw and Pochettino enjoyed success together at Southampton but the reunion won't last long.

Arriving as an Ineos project, United aren't going to cut their losses on Heaven just yet.

His strong passing ability will appeal to Pochettino and his coaches and he's worth a season of proper coaching to see how high or low his ceiling is.

Heaven can be reckless, particularly in his approach to tackling, but he's got a good physical profile and those who have worked with him have praised his approach to training and willingness to listen to coaches.

United are likely to go out and sign two new centre backs in the summer – at least they hope to – but Heaven should get a shot at development as a bit-part player.

Wholly ignored despite a left back crisis this season, Amass is widely expected to be out the door in January.

It is hard to blame him, either, given United's decision to keep him around has stunted his development.

Amass is a strong crosser of the ball and, in time, could develop into a full back in Pochettino's vision.

It has been revealed that but neither Amass nor Pochettino will have time to wait and see. With a left back high on the shopping list, to go with Dorgu's expected ascension, this relationship shouldn't last too long.

An academy player to keep an eye on.

Kamason has played both at right back and right wing for United's Under 21s and that plays massively into his hands in a bid to try and catch the eye of his latest manager.

The United youngster is a well-rounded full back that constantly looks to get forward, all while not neglecting his defensive responsibilities.

Kamason has trained regularly with the first team in recent months and that could be a sign of things to come under Pochettino, too.

United rolled the dice on Leon a year ago in a deal worth an initial £3.3million – but the move has not worked out at all.

The 19-year-old hasn't come close to making a first-team appearance and his agent has even suggested they are getting itchy feet despite sub-par performances for United's Under 21s.

Industry observers note that 'If there isn't a plan to break into the first team between December and January, we'll look for a way out for him,' Leon's representative Renato Bittar admitted. 'A loan somewhere where he can compete, get playing time, and return to Manchester.'.

Having observed the academy teams closer than most in recent seasons, Leon hasn't shown anywhere near enough to merit becoming a project player for Pochettino.

Mount left for United in the same summer Pochettino was hired by Chelsea, so their crossover was minimal.

How much say Pochettino had in that decision remains unclear, perhaps it was insignificant, but now they will finally work together.

Mount feels disposable, not least because he hasn't registered a single assist in the Premier League for United since joining in 2023 for £60million.

With so many options ahead of him in those inverted winger roles, and with Bruno Fernandes and Youri Tielemans preferred as No 10s, Mount needs shifting.

Bruno Fernandes (Midfielder, 32).

Contract talks have stalled in recent weeks and months but an ambitious new manager could swing momentum back towards reigning Player of the Year Fernandes staying at Old Trafford.

The way Pochettino platformed Christian Eriksen and Dele Alli at Tottenham, as well as Cole Palmer at Chelsea, suggests Fernandes will get the role he needs to be at his very best.

Recent findings suggest that fernandes' mobility, and ability to run beyond his centre forward, is a strength, as is his vision to supply team-mates in open play and at set-pieces. If Fernandes plays well, so do United, generally. Pochettino favours inverted attackers, so Fernandes could even start off the left if his manager wanted to position Matheus Cunha or Tielemans more centrally.

'He's given me the freedom to play my stuff and I like it when he frees you because I feel I can express my stuff more,' Palmer stated of Pochettino's coaching back in 2024.

'I'm loving it. Every day he's talking to you about different things, not just football things but life things as well. He's good at making you feel good and trying to get the best out of you.'.

That's music to the ears of Fernandes.

Pochettino's free-flowing approach could be exactly what is needed to keep Bruno Fernandes.

Pochettino knows all about Santos having worked with him at Chelsea when he was a teenager still finding his way.

The reports at that time, during a pre-season tour in North Carolina and Philadelphia, were that Santos' profile appealed to Pochettino, only for the club to go ahead and sanction loan moves to Nottingham Forest and then Strasbourg.

Santos is a summer arrival for £50m and will get more time to find his role in this United side.

He has enough talent to become a reliable deputy to Baleba as the deep-lying midfielder when everyone is fully fit.

Youri Tielemans (Midfielder, 29).

Tielemans is a high-IQ player that signed a five-year contract in the summer so, truthfully, won't be going anywhere.

That being said, Tielemans' running power isn't there and the demands of a Pochettino system, if he is still the same coach that bowed out at Chelsea, may make that secondary midfield role difficult.

It feels like Tielemans could be a specialist player that Pochettino uses in games where his side expect to dominate possession.

Tielemans' composure on the ball is superior to that of many of his team-mates and that's not a trait Pochettino will overlook quickly, even if he reportedly had reservations on a younger Tielemans when he was managing at Tottenham.

A substantial winner. The £70m summer signing needs to be used in the correct way to realise his potential and Pochettino's track record should be music to Baleba's ears.

Pochettino has typically liked one of his central midfielders to drop deep in possession to create a back three – see Eric Dier at Tottenham – and Baleba should be comfortable fulfilling that role.

Moises Caicedo and Wanyama are two other success stories in the deeper No6 role that Baleba should now thrive in under Pochettino's watch, with his combativeness and tackling making him a natural fit.

'Tactically, he has taught me a lot,' Wanyama previously remarked of Pochettino.

'Before, I was just thinking, "I'll just sit here and defend". But if you're playing for him, it's not only defending. You have to attack also. You have to know the right time. I have learned so much from him.'.

Now it's time for Baleba to study up and take his game to the next level.

Carlos Baleba has a had a slow start to life at United but a managerial change could unlock his potential.

It transpired that Pochettino wanted to make Ugarte his first signing at Chelsea, only for United to get in ahead of them for the Uruguayan.

Ugarte was all set to leave United in the summer were it not for a serious injury at the World Cup that left him sidelined for months.

Pochettino liked the profile of player he saw when Ugarte was scouted at Sporting Lisbon but he looks a different, far less effective, player in England.

Minds appear to be made up upstairs when it comes to moving on from Ugarte.

Where Baleba will need to drop deep, the other midfielder in Pochettino's system is the one who is expected to drive and bypass midfield blocks.

Pochettino will be acutely aware that Mainoo is extremely popular among United fans and while athleticism is often levelled against him as a weak point in his game, Pochettino will need to find a way of improving that while also nurturing his many talents.

Tottenham's Mousa Dembele was moulded by Pochettino from an attacking midfielder into a deep-lying controller, urged to dribble to break lines and open up the game.

Mainoo has many similar traits to others Pochettino has worked with, such as Weston McKennie with the US national team.

'They will get pushed in training more than the games they will be playing. It is all a mental thing,' former Southampton striker Rickie Lambert once noted.

If Mainoo can come through the initial boot camp, he can flourish.

Kobbie Mainoo is one of United's top talents and will stay but has to improve his physicality.

A better player than people give him credit for but one that really needs to put a full season together at first-team level to see where he is at.

That won't be under Pochettino at United but United, if they really believe he can be part of their future, need to find Fletcher a loan move where he can feature in 35-40 games.

Clubs in League One would be all over him.

Tyler Fletcher (Midfielder, 19).

The deep-lying midfielder that can drop in to form a back three is fundamental to how Pochettino wants to play and that's a style that would suit Tyler Fletcher, rather than the more attacking Jack.

Again, figures at United and up in Scotland, just want to see Fletcher get a run of games under his belt.

Kilmarnock wanted him in the summer, but United wanted to keep Fletcher in house.

If Pochettino and United really care about his career, he should be one of the first out the door on loan in January.

Senior academy figures are the most excited about Thwaites' potential, even if it would be unfair to expect him to make a major impact on the first team in the near future.

Technically his level is particularly high, a European pass-first, press-resistant game that will appeal to Pochettino and his coaches.

But physically there is a way to go, which should mean Thwaites is kept around as a project player.

Brought in as an Ineos project piece, after two mediocre loan spells in Switzerland with Lausanne, it's time to have Kone come back into the building and put him to work with a relentless coach like Pochettino.

Kone's twitchy game-style and desire to break through lines makes him something of a hybrid of players Pochettino has coached in the past.

Having watched him up close in the academy set-up before he went out on loan, and spoken to those who coached Kone then, it would be a massive gamble for Pochettino to put his trust in him.

But Kone's ceiling feels sky high. It's time to see if he can go into the lab and come out as a Dembele-Wanyama hybrid.

VERDICT: Keep as project player.

Cristian Orozco (Midfielder, 18).

Physically he has an advanced profile for his age but United have long preached that they want to take things slow as Orozco settles into life in England and gets a grip of the language.

He is neat and tidy on the ball and has shown an ability to zip passes through the lines but not enough to suggest an elevation to the first-team group.

Academy football doesn't develop players promptly enough so a carefully selected loan move, perhaps in a technical league like the Netherlands or Belgium, would be ideal.

He needs to look at how Pochettino used players like Lucas Moura and Eriksen in the past to see how he can take his game to the next level.

Cunha has a swagger about him that United like and while he was better suited to Ruben Amorim's system than he was Michael Carrick's, Pochettino's preference for narrow wide players, funnelling them into central areas while full backs create the width, means this managerial shift should play into his hands.

'Cunha is a maverick who does things that are hard to find in some players,' Amorim once said of the Brazilian.

'He plays with the ball, but he has an aura that can do something to the opponent's heads. And that is really notable.'.

It was recently suggested to Daily Mail Sport that a move for Rashford could be explored as early as January, with a desire to go back abroad.

A managerial change always puts things into flux and not least given that Pochettino said in 2022 that he'd 'always liked' Rashford, before adding: 'I think he's a great player. He just needs the confidence and for himself to believe, to put him at the top level. The quality is there for him.'.

Pochettino is unlikely to have changed an opinion as solid as that one in the years that followed and so it will be curious to see if Rashford could become the athletic, pressing No9 in Benjamin Sesko's absence.

Rashford wants to feel the love and has shown what he can do when his confidence is high. It isn't right now but don't bet against Pochettino showing him that love.

Rashford has been linked with another move away but could become a pressing No 9.

One of the more interesting profiles for Pochettino to consider.

On the face of it, Zirkzee lacks the intensity in the press and the mobility that Pochettino demands of his forwards.

Yet, Zirkzee can drop in, allowing the No10 to run in behind, which Pochettino values in a striker.

In the long term, expect Zirkzee to depart. In the short term, Pochettino may see him as a very specific tool to exploit certain opponents.

Tenacious defensively after improving immeasurably out of possession under Amorim, that's a big plus for Amad in the eyes of Pochettino.

He's among the glut of hybrid 10-wingers that United seem to stockpile and, once Sesko returns, Amad will find himself locked in a battle with Shea Lacey and Bryan Mbeumo for regular starts.

Amad's energy should give him the edge from day one to be a natural fit for Pochettino's high press.

Pochettino loves working with young players and Lacey is ready-made for that inverted winger style that the Argentine prefers, so he should be licking his lips at the prospect of more opportunities.

Lacey has played both off the right and as a No10 in academy teams and that stands him in good stead to operate in central areas, as well as isolate his full back one v one, which too many in this squad are not confident to do.

Lacey should be studying the development of Dele Alli under Pochettino and hoping he can bring his game on similarly.

Shea Lacey is (right) is a hugely promising youngster who will love working with Pochettino.

Like Cunha, Mbeumo looked a more natural fit in Amorim's two-10s system and there are similarities that could put him back in those positions under Pochettino.

He's played a lot as a No 9 and may need to deputise there for the time being but the long-term dilemma for Pochettino will be the battle between Mbeumo, Amad and Lacey cutting in from the right.

It's one of the few areas of the pitch where there will be decent competition for places.

Mbeumo will need to find a position and master it or he may be caught in between roles.

Injured until, most likely, the end of January and so it will take some time for Pochettino to get his teeth into Sesko's development.

The Slovenian feels very close to Pochettino's ideal No9 profile given his athleticism, physicality in the air, ability to press from the front and his instinctive finishing ability.

Benjamin Sesko could raise his level under a manager who routinely improves forwards.

Academy sources feel the teenager, who arrived for an initial £4million, has been unfairly criticised so far as he tries to adapt to a fresh club since moving up from Tottenham.

Thompson has picked up in recent academy games but in terms of his profile he looks more comfortable as a touchline winger, minus the blistering pace we usually see in that position.

His best bet is to remain in the academy and look towards a season-long loan next season.

One of the most intriguing academy prospects now that JJ Gabriel is closing in on a move to Real Madrid.

Ajayi looks physically capable of holding his own in first-team sessions and before a ball was kicked this term the development plan was to have him make a first-team debut before the season was out.

On-pitch failings may kick that can down the road but Ajayi is comfortable anywhere across the front line, has an acceleration that's invaluable and a technical level beyond his years.

Pochettino needs to take him under his wing to see what he can squeeze out of him before next summer.

VERDICT: Integrate into first-team training.

David Dunn predicts Burnley vs Blackburn Rovers scoreline and tells his former club how to hurt their rivals

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Blackburn Rovers head to Turf Moor off the back of their 2-1 win at home against West Ham last time out before the international break.
  • The Lancashire outfit are positioned in 13th place in the Championship table after their first 15 fixtures of the season.
  • Dunn, who had two separate spells at Ewood Park during his playing career, has delivered his score prediction ahead of the weekend via The Red Rose Divide on YouTube: “I’m going to go with 2-1 Blackburn.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Blackburn Rovers head to Turf Moor off the back of their 2-1 win at home against West Ham last time out before the international break. Attacking pair Andri Gudjohnsen and Dapo Afolayan got their goals against the Hammers as they secured an eye-catching three points.

The Lancashire outfit are positioned in 13th place in the Championship table after their first 15 fixtures of the season. They are only three points off the play-offs behind both QPR and Southampton.

Dunn, who had two separate spells at Ewood Park during his playing career, has delivered his score prediction ahead of the weekend via The Red Rose Divide on YouTube: “I’m going to go with 2-1 Blackburn. First goal scorer it would be daft not to pick Gudjohnsen but I feel like it might be a set piece. I think there could be some set pieces.”.

It has been revealed that blackburn Rovers have seen head coach Tony Mowbray take a step back this week due to health problems. Damien Johnson and Mike Dodds will take first-team duties for the time being.

Dunn believes Blackburn Rovers can hurt Burnley from set-pieces. Centre-backs Hayden Carter and Sean McLoughlin will head up the pitch for set pieces.

In a recent development, in striker Gudjohnsen, Rovers have one of the best attackers in the division at the moment. The 24-year-old, who is an Iceland international with 45 caps to his name, has 11 goals in 15 outings in all competitions in this campaign.

It has been revealed that todd Cantwell has flourished so far this term and he injects valuable quality into the team. He is out of contract next summer and his long-term situation needs addressing sooner rather than later.

Afolayan has also hit the ground running over recent times and can cause problems for opposition defenders. The ex-Bolton Wanderers man joined from St. Pauli last January and initially took a bit of time to find his feet.

Recent findings suggest that blackburn Rovers will be in confident mood after seeing off West Ham. They can’t afford to be complacent against Burnley though and will need to be at their best to get something, especially in a derby game.

Industry observers note that the Clarets were relegated from the Premier League earlier this year after they finished in the bottom three along with the Hammers and Wolves. They have made a poor start to this season and they are in the drop zone along with Preston North End and Derby County.

Fabio Celestini was appointed as their manager in late October after their decision to give Nicky Hayen the sack. He is yet to win in his first three matches, drawing two and losing one.

Carlo Ancelotti and Raphinha see red: Security separate furious Brazil stars from officials after shock 3-2 defeat by Japan - with manager and captain sent off in bad-tempered friendly

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (669 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 11:31 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 12:52 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Carlo Ancelotti hit out at an 'inexperienced' referee after the Brazil boss and captain Raphinha were sent off in the closing stages of their shock 3-2 defeat by Japan.
  • Security staff were required to enter the pitch at full time to separate players from the officials, with Brazil having been left furious over the nature of Japan's stoppage time winner.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By MICHAEL PAVITT, SPORTS REPORTER.

Published: 11:31 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 12:52 EST, 14 November 2026.

Carlo Ancelotti hit out at an 'inexperienced' referee after the Brazil boss and captain Raphinha were sent off in the closing stages of their shock 3-2 defeat by Japan.

Security staff were required to enter the pitch at full time to separate players from the officials, with Brazil having been left furious over the nature of Japan's stoppage time winner.

Ancelotti and Raphinha, who had been substituted, were among those to furiously protest following Tatsuhiro Sakamoto's late strike.

Singaporean referee Jansen Foo Chuan Hui had allowed play to continue after Takumi Minamino had made multiple challenges on Brazil midfielder Joao Gomes, before eventually coming away with the ball.

Amid Brazilian appeals for a foul, Japan rolled out a late attack with Sakamoto ultimately lifting the ball over goalkeeper Pedro Morisco.

Brazilian protests continued despite Japan's winner being confirmed by VAR, with Ancelotti and Raphinha being shown red cards by the referee for their reactions.

Security staff intervened after Brazil stars confronted the referee after their 3-2 defeat by Japan.

Carlo Ancelotti was sent off as Brazil were beaten in stoppage time in their friendly in Singapore.

Ancelotti criticised the 'inexperienced' referee following the match and revealed he had been told he had been sent off for failing to control his bench.

🚨🚨| Raphinha and Carlo Ancelotti have been SENT OFF for Protesting. 🟥😳 pic.twitter.com/YoXrZW9N0U.

'He gave me the red card because he remarked I was not able to control the bench, and that all the players were on the field, that is the reason,' Ancelotti said.

Ancelotti added: 'A pity the result, because we don't like to lose the game, but we have to look at what we did well. There are many things. Some players who played for the first time, who showed good quality. For 70 minutes, the team was good.

'The result, obviously, is conditioned by the attitude of the referee, who did not blow the whistle.

'But it's not his fault; it was a high-level match, and I think he didn't have the experience to manage this type of match.'.

Barcelona star Raphinha claimed post-match that Brazil had also been angered over a potential handball in the build-up to Japan's opening goal, as well as seeing a penalty appeal waved away.

'First of all, I'd like to take this opportunity to apologise for my behaviour and for being sent off,' Raphinha told Globo.

In a recent development, 'Sometimes it's hard to keep calm, especially after what I felt were so many refereeing errors during the match. I tried to speak to him several times, and not once did I feel he was open to discussion. I believe that he made many errors throughout the game, and that is unacceptable.

Sources indicate that 'In my view, their first goal involved a foul where the opponent took the ball off me with his hand. I think it's a foul, but I can understand why it wasn't given based on the current law.

Brazil captain Raphinha was also dismissed amid their protests over Japan's winning goal.

Brazil had been convinced there had been a foul in the build-up to Tatsuhiro Sakamoto's winner.

'Then there was the penalty in the first half, in my opinion it was a penalty, but he mentioned no. Then, for their third goal, there was a clear foul on Joao Gomes. With the help of VAR, he eventually allowed the goal. It's very difficult not to talk about the refereeing.'.

Brazil had fallen 2-0 down in the friendly with Takefusa Kubo and Keito Nakamura scoring in the opening 20 minutes at Singapore's National Stadium.

Real Madrid winger Vinicius Jr scored twice to level the match before Sakamoto's controversial late winner.

It is the second time Japan have beaten Brazil 3-2 in the past 18 months, but the five-time world champions did win 2-1 in their last-32 meeting at this summer's World Cup.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, championship sides will have eyes firmly on potential targets for the January transfer window.
  • In a recent development, writing on X, Daily Mail reporter Tom Collomosse states that ‘several’ Championship sides are interested in signing the 18-year-old defender on loan.
  • Recent findings suggest that lienou is yet to make his senior debut but has been a regular for the Whites’ U21s after previous spells in the Liverpool, Everton and Manchester City youth setups.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, championship sides will have eyes firmly on potential targets for the January transfer window. Clubs across the division will be eager to add players who can aid their promotion pushes or survival fights, and one man attracting early attention is Leeds United prospect Jayden Lienou.

In a recent development, writing on X, Daily Mail reporter Tom Collomosse states that ‘several’ Championship sides are interested in signing the 18-year-old defender on loan. Leeds United are ‘very excited’ about Lienou’s potential, as he has been training with the first team since February and has been involved in Wales’ senior picture too.

Recent findings suggest that lienou is yet to make his senior debut but has been a regular for the Whites’ U21s after previous spells in the Liverpool, Everton and Manchester City youth setups. He primarily plays as a left-back but has been used as a centre-back in a 3-4-3 as well.

Recent findings suggest that lienou is a versatile left-sided defender. As noted beforehand, he mainly plays as a left-back, but he can drop into a back three as a central defender or move further forward into a wing-back role.

He has had a strong footballing education in a string of top academies, but his performances for Leeds United’s U21s have really confirmed him as one to watch. It speaks volumes that he has been around the first-team squads for both his club and country.

Recent findings suggest that lienou has the speed and energy to operate in a flexible role on the left-hand side. His defensive anticipation and strong tackling in one-on-one situations help him adapt to a more defence-focused style as well.

At only 18, he will need time to settle into the senior game and adjust to the pace and power of Championship football. However, his training involvement at Leeds and with Wales means he will have a good idea of the task awaiting him if a loan deal is struck in the winter.

The Championship is an excellent proving ground for young Premier League talents. There have been countless loan success stories over the years, with the 2026/27 season seeing Rio Cardines and Pierce Charles star at Bristol City and QPR respectively, amongst others.

Leeds United will want Lienou to go and play regularly wherever he goes. It means that the club chiefs must carefully weigh up the style of play and existing left-sided defender options for all of those interested in signing him on loan.

At his age, Lienou can benefit from being around a senior squad on matchdays more regularly. He can learn from established senior players at the level and hopefully have a positive impact on whoever he joins.

#49674. £329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

£329m spent and still no goals for sorry Tottenham

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 21 min read (4127 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~21 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on fresh players really does take some doing.
  • Recent findings suggest that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium.
  • It has been revealed that A team reimagined, a manager freshly rolled out and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tottenham Hotspur have never before in the club’s history begun a league season without scoring a single goal in the first four games, although having done so after spending £329m on fresh players really does take some doing.

Recent findings suggest that “Please score a goal!” was the homemade sign from two Spurs fans upon which the television cameras lingered at the end of the game, although the jaunty felt-tip design and glued-on team crest were rather upbeat compared to the gloom of the stadium. Spurs have tried to outrun their past but it just keeps catching up with them.

It has been revealed that A team reimagined, a manager freshly rolled out and yet they are back in the same grip of anxiety that accompanied them on two consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons. By the end of this they might have been glad to escape with a single point against Everton, the one team in the Premier League who closed the window with a net transfer profit.

In a recent development, for Roberto De Zerbi, there was another passionate defence of his team afterwards. “The people, the fans already understand if I make excuses or not,” he mentioned. “I came last season when the s--- was like this”, he gestured to a level somewhere around the midpoint of his forehead. “I have always been… not positive but realistic. I am sorry for the result that it’s not immediately the improvement. We played as a team. We didn’t score. We didn’t win [but] we played as a team.”.

In a recent development, indeed he co-opted the Italian term “sbloccare” to describe his team’s problem. They simply need to unlock – or unblock – the team and the goals would flow. He joked that in Italy he would be lauded for two consecutive clean sheets in this game and the previous one against Nottingham Forest. “What did you write?” he demanded of one of the Italian newspaper correspondents. “You have the passport.”.

In a recent development, spurs have one last game at home this month, on Saturday against Aston Villa, to end the streak in September. They were into the second half before the first attempt on target that obliged Jordan Pickford to make a save – Mateus Fernandes’s shot slapping limply against the Everton goalkeeper’s gloves to ironic cheers from the home fans.

Recent findings suggest that at the end De Zerbi could not contain his frustration, unable to wait until he reached the privacy of the dressing room to tell Mathys Tel where he had gone wrong. He did so with the Spurs substitute still wiping the sweat from his brow on the pitch. The player did not look at all impressed. De Zerbi said later that he was simply reminding his player of what it took to play as a central striker.

Sources indicate that “There is a term in Italian, ‘sbloccare’ that literally translates as ‘unblock’… I know we can score goals and win games. We have to respect the history of the players – if you forget [Dominic] Solanke and [Omar] Marmoush the others haven’t scored many in their careers. I think we can find the goals with the quality of the players.”.

Spurs play Liverpool at Anfield in the Carabao Cup on Tuesday before Villa a week today. The Spurs record at home is dismal. In the last 35 games they have won just five, drawn 10 and lost a remarkable 20. This new stadium has become a problem for the team in it – or maybe it is the other way around.

Sources indicate that A good result for Everton, who were under pressure for most of the first half but had much the better of it after the break. David Moyes’s team finished the game with more shots on target than the home team. Moyes managed the game well and trusted his team to withstand the Spurs possession in the first half until they reached a point where Everton could start to push back.

Hard to pick out any major chances – it was that kind of game – but Brennan Johnson should have won it for the away team in the second half. The ball was cut back to him by Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and the former Spurs man skied his shot.

Some surprised faces then when Moyes remarked later that he had expected a lot more from his team. He acknowledged the resilience in defence and the importance of the clean sheet. “We played well enough,” he said, “but when we had the ball we turned it over more often than we should have done.”.

Recent findings suggest that the game had started with Vitaliy Mykolenko being tortured by the pace of Sávio and ended with the Ukrainian left-back being given the man of the match award. Like many of his team-mates, he had hung in there. There was another fine performance from Jarrad Branthwaite at centre-half and Moyes said that he hoped it might earn him a place in the England squad. “He is still finding his way back from injury,” Moyes said, “it would be great if he could get a call-up.”.

In the directors’ box were the usual pained expressions of Vinai Venkatesham, the Spurs chief executive, and chairman Peter Charrington. They sat alongside Vivienne Lewis, daughter of the patriarch Joe. There is a certain fatigue about the home crowd when faced with afternoons like this which suggests they have seen so much that the bar is quite high – or low – to provoke a really splenetic response. Perhaps it is just too early in the season although the final whistle was met with boos.

The first shot on target of the entire game for either side was a free-kick struck by James Garner in added time at the end of the first half. Spurs had started at a ferocious pace although they could not sustain it.

De Zerbi complained about the pre-season injuries on tour in Australia and also the lack of time he had to integrate Sávio and Marmoush. He said that his team were not in the right “physical condition”.

“We played very well in the first 30 minutes and maybe the energy and the fact we didn’t score – we lost confidence.” By the end, he had sent on James Maddison, Tel, Lucas Bergvall and Mohammed Kudus to little avail. Everton looked more likely to win it.

In a recent development, speaking to Sky Sports, the Everton defender said: “You look at the game from the start, they put us under pressure and we had to dig deep to stay in the game. Then we grew into the game towards the end of the first half and highlighted that mentality again in the second half.

It has been revealed that “We had chances to win the game as well. The backs to the wall mentality will help us go a long way. If we can keep clean sheets, you can go a long way in the league. But it’s not just us the defenders. It’s the whole team working hard. It’s a team effort.”.

"I feel like we could've taken three points" James Tarkowski speaks after his sides draw with Spurs 🎙️ pic.twitter.com/Wdj3N5hk8l.

"Six hours and we've not scored a goal? It's a DISGRACE" 😬Ashley Young notes that the Spurs players will need to have conversations about their lack of threat going forward ❌ pic.twitter.com/0KNomGEavx.

"Absolutely diabolical" 😬Jamie Redknapp on Spurs not scoring in their first four Premier League games 😳 pic.twitter.com/48Nbxymlev.

Tottenham failed to take the attacking initiative or create any notable chances. De Zerbi used multiple forward players in a host of attacking positions, but no one could find the breakthrough.

Sources indicate that boos ring around the ground as Spurs and Everton both have to settle for a point. Tottenham’s winless start to the season continues, while Everton’s unbeaten run remains intact. Spurs haven’t managed a goal in six hours of Premier League football across the 2026-27 campaign. Tottenham sit 17th with two points. Everton are up to seventh and will certainly take the draw.

FULL-TIME: The points are shared between Spurs and Everton at Tottenham Hotspur stadium 🤝 pic.twitter.com/HwPuKI3Ajh.

According to recent reports, dewsbury-Hall’s deflected effort flies out for a corner. Everton can’t make the most of the resulting set piece and Tottenham survive.

There will be three minutes of added time. Are we set for late drama at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium?

Pickford makes an error as his poor clearance is intercepted by Maddison. The ball is eventually worked to Bergvall, whose curling effort is parried away by the Everton goalkeeper.

Jordan Pickford gets down well to deny Lucas Bergvall! 🧤 pic.twitter.com/59uoHTqto6.

Industry observers note that tosin comes on for his Spurs debut as he replaces Gray. Can anyone be Tottenham’s hero and find a late winner?

Sources indicate that garner is booked after he clatters into Savio. Everton have produced a tough and disciplined defensive perfomance so far.

It has been revealed that spurs are now enjoying a sustained period of possession. They’re waiting to fashion a significant chance and end their wait for a top-flight goal in the 2026-27 season.

De Zerbi makes another change as Maddison enters the action with applause from the Spurs faithful. He replaces Marmoush. It looks like Tel is now operating as a false nine.

Johnson misses a huge chance! Dewsbury-Hall fires a low cross into his path and Johnson takes the chance with a first-time shot, but he slices his effort and it goes over the bar. He’s got to do better from that range inside the penalty area.

That opportunity is Johnson’s last action of the match as he comes off for Hackney. O’Brien is also introduced, replacing Maitland-Niles.

Recent findings suggest that that was the chance. Dewsbury-Hall rolls it into the path of Spurs’ Europa League final winner Brennan Johnson and he skied it. He hasn’t scored since he left Spurs in January for Palace.

"What a chance this was!"Brennan Johnson had the chance to put Everton in front against his former club 😯 pic.twitter.com/fUi7t6hX7t.

It has been revealed that everton look like the far likelier side to break the deadlock. De Zerbi’s changes have done little to affect the game. Marmoush is cutting a very frustrated figure up top for Spurs.

Sources indicate that bergvall finds Savio with a whipped cross. The winger tries to help the ball back into the danger zone, but Pickford reacts quickly and collects possession.

Dewsbury-Hall picks up the game’s first yellow card after catching Tonali with a late sliding challenge.

What is Kinsky doing?! The goalkeeper’s dreadful pass which was intended for Tonali is intercepted by Dewsbury-Hall, who tries to slide a low effort through Kinsky’s legs. The Tottenham man redeems himself with a crucial save to keep the scoreline goalless. The hosts are living so dangerously. Kinsky needs to wake up.

According to recent reports, antonín Kinský redeems himself after Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall fails to take advantage! 😮 pic.twitter.com/nuKZju90Wz.

Moyes responds with a straight swap on the wing as Grealish comes on for George.

Sources indicate that enter: Grealish. He is on for Tyrique George. Surprised that Brennan Johnson survived that change. He has struggled to make an impression.

Following Spurs’ reshuffle, it looks like Savio will stay out wide on the right, with Tel on the left. Kudus will sit as the central playmaker behind Marmoush, who is now the lone frontman.

De Zerbi orders a much-needed triple change as Kudus, Tel and Bergvall replace Solanke, Fernandes and Bentancur.

Jack Grealish has long since stopped the warm-up on the touchline and is now just staring at the game in expectation of his introduction.

Industry observers note that A couple of chances for Everton. Spurs have survived but they look so vulnerable when Everton turn over possession. Crowd could turn soon. Almost reached the hour-mark on matchday 4 and still no Spurs’ Premier League goal.

According to recent reports, the start of Spurs’ second-half performance is alarmingly similar to their display against Newcastle two weeks ago. That day, Tottenham allowed Newcastle to seize the initiative and they netted two second-half goals without reply. Everton are gaining confidence as Spurs continue to lack courage or threat. The crowd is getting more and more restless.

Tottenham fail to clear a corner and the ball lands at George’s feet. The Everton winger shoots but his fierce drive is blocked by Bentancur. The whole of Spurs’ bench is warming up. The visitors right now have the momentum and the hosts look nervous.

Everton are looking threatening once again as George attempts to thread a pass through to Johnson on the counter-attack, but Van de Ven is there to clear.

Industry observers note that george does brilliantly to escape away from Gray and floats a cross towards the back post. Barry rises highest and his close-range header is blocked by Kinsky. The Tottenham goalkeeper didn’t know much about it, but that’s a massive stop. Undoubtedly the game’s most dangerous moment in front of goal so far.

According to recent reports, spurs’ first shot has arrived! Unfortunately, Fernandes’ tame long-range effort is easily gathered by Pickford. There were some sarcastic cheers from the Tottenham fans as Fernandes took aim. They clearly want more attacking inspiration from their players.

Recent findings suggest that ironic cheers as Spurs have their first shot on target. It has taken them until the start of the second half and it would be hard to say Fernandes stung the palms of Pickford.

Recent findings suggest that we are back under way for the second half. Everton and Spurs are both unchanged at the break. With the anxiety building in the stadium as the game remains goalless, how long will De Zerbi wait before making a change?

It has been revealed that an uneventful first half of football comes to a close. In a game lacking rhythm, creativity and attacking spark, nothing separates Tottenham and Everton at the break. Spurs’ search for a first Premier League goal this season continues.

There will be two added minutes. Everton have a free kick on the edge of Spurs’ penalty area. Garner and Dewsbury-Hall are standing over it. The former Manchester United and Nottingham Forest midfielder takes it and his effort bounces in front of Kinsky, who pushes it out for a corner.

James Garner free-kick pushed away by Kinsky is the game’s first attempt on target.

There has not been a single attempt on target at 40:27 from either team. Spurs have had the best of it but even so. That’s a poor return.

Another attack fizzles out for Spurs. Substitute Jack Grealish engaging in some badinage with home fans as he warms up. He famously agreed a move to Spurs in 2018, called off at the eleventh hour when Aston Villa were sold to the current ownership.

In a recent development, that is so poor from Fernandes. The summer signing’s overhit corner drifts out for a goal kick. Suddenly, Spurs’ attacking play has fallen quite flat.

Industry observers note that pickford does well to intercept Robertson’s inviting low cross. The left back needed Solanke or Marmoush to make a darting near-post run there to give him more options.

Spurs are bossing this game but on the rare occasions Everton escape you do wonder if they might score.

In a recent development, tottenham are roared on by the home support to move the ball a bit quicker going forward. Out of possession, Everton almost revert to a back five, with Garner dropping very deep near to Tarkowski and Branthwaite.

Industry observers note that tonali picks out Gray with a pinpoint pass. Garner is alert to the danger and tracks back to clear, stopping Gray from getting a one-on-one opportunity.

Maitland-Niles does very well to dispossess Tonali in a dangerous area, allowing Barry to tee up Dewsbury-Hall, but his shot is smothered by the Spurs defence. Mykolenko then chips a cross into a box, but it’s tapped behind for a corner by Robertson. Moyes will certainly be encouraged by this side’s resurgence over the last 10 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that there is a break in play here with Gray down and receiving treatment after a collision. He appears to be holding his lower back. The Tottenham man gingerly gets back to his feet and trudges off the pitch.

According to recent reports, gray down for some extended treatment. Richarlison in the stands. Spurs in danger of losing early momentum.

After Spurs’ fast start, Everton have grown into the contest over the last five minutes and are getting on the ball far higher up the pitch.

Recent findings suggest that garner’s corner is cleared by Spurs, but only as far as Maitland-Niles. In similar range to where he scored that stunning equaliser against Manchester United, the former Arsenal man shoots, but his attempt fizzes well wide.

Spurs are really flowing here. Finding the balls through the lines and real speed when they attack Everton. Substantial question is whether they can convert that into goals. Van Hecke and Fernandes both had chances.

Sávio has had a fine start to the game. Mykolenko in for a long afternoon. Spurs have looked dangerous and should be 1-0 up.

It has been revealed that tonali finds Savio with a deep cross, leaving Pickford in no-man’s land. The Brazilian keeps the ball in play and it loops up, just out of Marmoush’s reach.

Robertson floats a teasing delivery into Van Hecke at the back post, but the centre-back directs his half-volley over the bar from close range.

Spurs then burst forward again through Savio, who feeds Fernandes. The playmaker’s low drive is heroically blocked by Tarkowski as Everton continue to hold on (just about).

As expected, it’s Tottenham with all the early possession, with Everton sitting very deep and soaking up the early pressure. Marmoush turns Armstrong and wins a free-kick in a dangerous area.

They’re under way in north London, the hosts are in their lily-white and navy kit, with Everton in their grey/dirty green (is that a colour?!) away number.

Greetings from N17. It’s a wonderful, warm late summer evening. As expected there is the usual foreboding from the home fans. Two defeats and one draw. The mood will sour further if Spurs do not win today. No Porro or Udogie so Archie Gray, ever adaptable, starts at right-back again.

Everton are undefeated with five points from three games. They have a decent 16/17 players but it is the reserves beyond that which everyone is concerned about. Grealish and Dibling on the bench give them two potential game-changers. Spurs’ squad looks very strong on the team-sheet. A full bench of experienced pros and no fillers. On the pitch it has been less convincing.

Brennan Johnson spent two years at Tottenham and scored the winning goal in the 1-0 Europa League final victory over Manchester United in May 2025, ending the club’s 17-year trophy drought.

After a short, disappointing spell at Crystal Palace, Johnson joined Everton last month, with Dwight McNeil moving in the opposite direction.

The Welsh winger starts for Everton today. Could he hurt his previous employers on a day where they desperately need a win?

Brennan in the building. 💙 pic.twitter.com/94GgAY8c56.

Midfielder took exception to negativity surrounding club after moves for players on deadline day failed to materialise.

“We signed Jack [Grealish], which was nice, and I’d been speaking to him,” states Dewsbury-Hall, sitting in a café at the club’s Finch Farm training base. “But I had seen all the stuff [online], all the meltdowns about this and that and, in all honestly, it annoyed me a bit.

Sources indicate that “I get where people are coming from. Everyone wants to sign everyone and have the perfect squad, but there are still 19 lads in this building who are going to hopefully take this club to good things this year. That was getting disregarded. I was seeing people saying: ‘We’ll be lucky to stay up this year.’.

“What message is that sending to the lads who are already here? I’m not blaming anyone. We get it. It didn’t work. But let’s all be positive – right, it’s done, bang, let’s go. That’s what we’ve been trying to say in the dressing room.”.

Earlier this week, Mykhailo Mudryk picked up an ankle injury in training which has ruled the Chelsea loanee out of action for as long as two months.

The winger only made his debut for Tottenham as a late substitute against Nottingham Forest last week, but his attempt to rebuild his career following his anti-doping ban has been dealt a major blow.

Folarin Balogun’s proposed £39m move from Monaco collapsed on transfer deadline day, Richarlison’s return to the club didn’t materialise and Beto was sold to Fiorentina, leaving Thierno Barry as Everton’s only recognised striker.

Nottingham Forest’s pursuit of academy product Harrison Armstrong ruffled the fans’ feathers, while Iliman Ndiaye was sold to Manchester City for £60m.

Dwight McNeil, Tim Iroegbunam, Nathan Patterson, Adam Aznou and Idrissa Gueye were also allowed to leave.

Merlin Rohl and Tyrique George made their loans permanent, while Brennan Johnson, Hayden Hackney and Christian Norgaard were also added to the squad.

Summer signing Ainsley Maitland-Niles and Vitaliy Mykolenko are David Moyes’ only options at full-back.

Overall, there were a number of solid additions, just not enough of them to cover all the departures.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van de Ven, Van Hecke, Robertson; Tonali, Bentancur, Fernandes; Savio, Solankem, Marmoush.

Subs: Dubravka, Tosin, Senesi, Gallagher, Maddison, Tel, Bergvall, Kudus, Davies.

Everton: Pickford; Maitland-Niles, Tarkowski, Brathwaite, Mykolenko; Armstrong, Garner; Johnson, Dewsbury-Hall, George; Barry.

Subs: Travers, O’Brien, Keane, King, Alcaraz, Graham, Hackney, Dibling, Grealish.

Recent findings suggest that after scoring that last-minute leveller against Manchester United last time out, Ainsley Maitland-Niles is promoted to the starting 11 and replaces Merlin Rohl. Brennan Johnson returns to his former club and starts, while Jack Grealish is on the bench.

Sources indicate that roberto De Zerbi has made four alterations from last weekend’s stalemate with Nottingham Forest. Dominic Solanke, Mateus Fernandes, Archie Gray and Andy Robertson all come into the line-up. Pedro Porro and Destiny Udogie are out injured, while Conor Gallagher and Mathys Tel are relegated to the bench. Tosin Adarabioyo and James Maddison are also among the substitutes.

Our Spurs side to take on Everton 👊🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/n637s7swiD.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Everton in the capital.

Sources indicate that are Tottenham in must-win territory already? It may seem reactionary and premature, but after spending £380m in the summer to revamp an underperforming squad, Tottenham sit inside the relegation zone, with just one point and zero goals scored in three games.

Roberto De Zerbi’s men opened the 2026-27 top-flight season with worrying back-to-back defeats to Brentford and Newcastle United, before ending their losing streak last weekend thanks to a goalless draw against Nottingham Forest.

This game gives Tottenham another opportunity to reverse their dreadful home form. Last season, Spurs managed just three league wins at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium and lost 10. The recent 2-0 loss against Newcastle was a painful reminder of Spurs’ shortcomings at home, but they’ll be expected to be authoritative and seize the initiative here today. A much-needed three points would be the perfect remedy to ease the pressure and unwanted attention on De Zerbi and his squad.

Meanwhile, Everton have made an unbeaten start to the season, accumulating five points from their first three league matches. David Moyes’ side looked set for defeat last time out, when they were trailing Manchester United 2-1 at the Hill Dickinson Stadium heading into stoppage time, until Ainsley Maitland-Niles’ stunning 96th-minute equaliser salvaged a draw.

In a recent development, alongside drama on the pitch, there has also been noise off it. A bizarre transfer window has left Everton with a serious lack of depth up top and in both full-back positions. Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall responded to the fans’ negativity over this situation, saying their meltdowns “annoyed” him.

Nevertheless, they arrive in North London with all eyes on Tottenham and if the hosts can find a first league victory this season.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news coming shortly.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 12:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:14 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • In an age where much of the football on show in the English Premier League is so robotic as to be almost unwatchable, flashes of individual brilliance are increasingly becoming things to be cherished.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 12:41 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:14 EST, 14 November 2026.

In an age where much of the football on show in the English Premier League is so robotic as to be almost unwatchable, flashes of individual brilliance are increasingly becoming things to be cherished.

Across his time at Liverpool and Bournemouth, Ben Gannon-Doak has sporadically distinguished himself as someone who can light up a game by doing something out of the blue and out of the ordinary.

As many a defender will testify, that electric burst of pace across a short distance makes him unplayable at times. He has an X-factor which sets him apart from the crowd.

What a shame that injuries have restricted his number of appearances to this point. Since moving south from Celtic in 2022, including a loan spell with Middlesbrough, Gannon-Doak has played fewer than 50 times.

At the very time in his career when he could have done with smoothing off the rough edges, he’s spent far too long rehabilitating from one setback or another.

In the build-up to Friday’s match with North Macedonia, Sebastien Pocognoli spoke about how encouraged he was that the player was finally seeing more game time on the south coast, partly as a result of the team’s maiden voyage in Europe.

Ben Gannon-Doak started in a right wing-back role and had an energetic yet frustrating night.

The hope of all concerned was that the recent run of matches which the winger had so evidently needed would translate into a more accomplished display in a Scotland jersey. Alas, this proved to be wishful thinking.

Even against very ordinary opposition, Gannon-Doak’s display proved to be another frustrating watch for the Tartan Army.

Sources indicate that time and time again, he brought them to the edge of their seats by facing up a white jersey and seemingly disappearing in a puff of smoke towards the line. Rarely, however, did the end product materialise.

For a winger with such blinding speed to continually struggle with the all-important final ball is a difficult thing to repeatedly witness.

Industry observers note that we shall never know, of course, if the player’s crossing ability would be better by this stage if he hadn’t endured such wretched luck with injuries. But you suspect it’s now just about as good as it’s ever going to be.

The trouble for Pocognoli is that the quality of the delivery from wing-backs into the penalty box is arguably the most vital facet of his preferred 3-4-3 system.

When it breaks down, as it did so often against the group outsiders, the whole thing threatens to grind to a halt.

Gannon-Doak's crossing remains an area of concern for Scotland given his wide position.

On his record-equalling 102nd cap, Andy Robertson was also guilty of being wasteful on the other flank. Given we know what the skipper has delivered down the years, though, we can write that off as merely a bad night at the office.

The difference with Gannon-Doak is that we’ve rarely seen him tear it up on the flank in a Scotland jersey. So much pace and potential. Not enough positive outcomes when it comes to delivering crosses. In 21 matches, he has three assists and one goal. Those aren’t great numbers.

Just how long do you persevere with a player who doesn’t look to have the requisite skill set for such a specialised and vital position?

Recent findings suggest that aaron Hickey clearly doesn’t have the pace of the man who he replaced late on, yet he’s hardly a slouch. He is, though, more switched on defensively. And he does know how to cross a football.

It was telling that Gannon-Doak’s most positive contribution of the night against the group outsiders came when he left his station to move infield and take Oli McBurnie’s pass in his stride with the score standing at one-apiece.

According to recent reports, his surge towards the goal initially looked like it had been hampered by a heavy touch only for VAR to correctly identify that he’d been impeded by the goalkeeper. He earned his corn in that moment.

John McGinn’s conversion from 12 yards, his second goal of the night, spared Pocognoli’s blushes after a display which didn’t exactly inspire.

That sequence of play certainly raised the possibility that Gannon-Doak could be utilised to better effect in another role.

Gannon-Doak's forward burst led to the award of a penalty and hinted at an alternative role.

Recent findings suggest that if played more centrally, his crossing – undoubtedly his weak spot – would not be such an issue. But the acceleration and driving runs would still be there to cause chaos in and around the penalty box. That will always be his strong suit.

To get the best out of him, maybe the manager needs to redefine him.

It has been revealed that any redeployment would, obviously, create another issue. If Pocognoli remains wedded to the current system, it seems likely that Billy Gilmour and Lewis Ferguson will occupy the two holding berths.

Ahead of them, and behind the main striker, McGinn and Scott McTominay are virtually undroppable. It might be the case then, that Gannon-Doak is eventually utilised as an impact sub. Yet, it would not be a blueprint without its merits.

He’s got a part to play in this set-up. Probably just not where he’s at the moment being positioned.

Recent findings suggest that you’d be surprised, frankly, if he started in St Gallen on Monday. Switzerland are a far superior side to North Macedonia, already assured of promotion to League A by topping the section and looking to end this campaign with a flourish against a Scotland side they beat comfortably at Hampden.

They’ll ask far more questions of Pocognoli’s side. It feels like a task more suited to Hickey.

Scotland, collectively, will need to buck up their ideas if they are to stand any chance of emerging with a positive outcome or, at the least, some credit.

Scotland fans are desperate to see Gannon-Doak succeed but a little change might be needed.

There was a flatness to Friday’s performance, especially in a first half in which the much-vaunted high-press was conspicuous by its absence.

The passing was too safe and predictable. The tempo was low and the play was unimaginative. By half-time, the visitors had fashioned the better chance when Enis Bardhi smashed the ball into the side net.

According to recent reports, scotland were markedly better after the turnaround. After Billy Gilmour’s scarcely believable miss, they were deserving of the opener which came when McGinn burst into the box and lashed home after fine work from Che Adams.

Stemming straight from a corner, North Macedonia’s equaliser – which ended their eight-game goal drought – asked a serious question of Pocognoli’s players.

To their credit, they stepped up with Gannon-Doak’s foray into the box causing the moment of indecision on which the game swung.

Sources indicate that the manner of a first Hampden win for Pocognoli won’t live long in the memory. The fervent hope is that it proves to be the start of something.

Welshman and Premier League coach among two early contenders to replace Vitor Matos as Swansea City boss

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It has been revealed that swansea City saw head coach Vitor Matos’ departure confirmed on Wednesday.
  • The hunt for Matos’ replacement is on, and talkSPORT reporter Alex Crook states Welsh boss Rob Edwards and Liverpool first-team coach Tommy Elphick are contenders.
  • It has been revealed that edwards is out of work and would not require compensation.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that swansea City saw head coach Vitor Matos’ departure confirmed on Wednesday. The Portuguese boss has left to take charge of RC Strasbourg, with the Swans receiving a compensation fee of around £5m and placing Leon Britton, Kris O’Leary and potentially Ashley Williams in charge on an interim basis.

The hunt for Matos’ replacement is on, and talkSPORT reporter Alex Crook states Welsh boss Rob Edwards and Liverpool first-team coach Tommy Elphick are contenders. The fresh news comes after reputable fanzine the Swansea Independent stated early talks with Edwards were held, and Elphick would be ‘open to discussions’.

It has been revealed that edwards is out of work and would not require compensation. Elphick’s role in Andoni Iraola’s backroom staff at Anfield means the Swans would have to pay a fee to bring him to South Wales if they wish.

Edwards and Elphick are two intriguing candidates in Swansea City’s search for a boss.

Of the two, Edwards is the most obvious. The Welshman is experienced at Championship level from his spells with Watford, Luton Town and Middlesbrough, and he has promotion pedigree to his name from his time with the Hatters. He had Boro flying too, before an ultimately ill-fated move to Wolves.

Like Matos, he favours high-intensity football, and his use of wide players at Luton Town could see him use the Swans’ squad effectively.

At the other end of the spectrum, Elphick has no senior management experience. He has emerged as a highly regarded coach since retiring in 2021, starting out in the Bournemouth youth setup before stepping into the senior side with Gary O’Neill and retaining his role after Andoni Iraola’s arrival.

Sources indicate that iraola took him to Liverpool with him in the summer. The fact he has never been the lead man in the dugout means we can’t know what to expect from his tactical proposal, but if his principles are aligned with Iraola’s, expect fast ball progression and aggressive pressing.

According to recent reports, swansea City will be frustrated to lose another manager, just as they started to really build to something special. The same thing happened when Russell Martin was poached by Southampton.

Sources indicate that the Swans made great strides under Matos’ lead, so ideally they need a head coach who will oversee a similar tactical blueprint. It will help them work well with the existing squad and should limit teething problems after an unforeseen change in the dugout.

Swansea City will be carefully weighing up a number of candidates but there will be an eagerness to replace Matos as soon and efficiently as possible to limit how much it disrupts their season.

#49649. Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions

📅 12 Sep 2026 • ⏱️ 23m • 📚 Deep Dive (4555 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Co ↗ Open Full Page

Former Geordie Guimaraes taunts Sunderland fans as Arsenal show mark of champions

📅 12 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 23 min read (4555 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~23 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands.
  • Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality.
  • So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that bruno Guimarães cupped his ears and had a plastic cup thrown at him as the abuse came down from the stands. Despite the missiles, the Brazilian wore a look that made it clear he was very much enjoying his first goal in an Arsenal shirt.

Recent findings suggest that mikel Arteta has laid bare his quirky management techniques so his players are ready for any eventuality. Late meals and making the dressing room hotter are among his tricks, although nothing can prepare a player having 40,000 fans calling you a “sad Geordie b------”.

So it was a sweet moment for Guimarães, even more so after coming just after Sunderland had a penalty saved. Just 121 seconds after Enzo Le Fée had his spot kick tipped on to a post by David Raya, Guimarães was rubbing salt into the wound with a stunning long-range strike that went in off the crossbar.

Enzo Le Fée is denied by David Raya from the spot 😳🧤📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/wnoMCDVh88.

Bruno Guimarães silences the Stadium of Light with a BEAUTY 🥵🚀📺 Stream with TNT Sports on HBO Max pic.twitter.com/zQHSSLxC3o.

The former Newcastle captain gave the perfect response after being taunted his old rivals. “It was a beautiful goal,” he said. “Everyone knows my past, I had an amazing history at Newcastle. But now I’m trying to create a new history here and I have started on the right foot.”.

What an key week it has been for Arsenal, who have shown their squad depth by winning in Napoli then travelling to the Stadium of Light and extending their perfect start to the season to six games.

According to recent reports, other teams with aspirations of the title dropped points earlier in the day, while Arteta could battle to a win with key players brought back into the team and Guimarães coming off the bench at half-time. A trip in the Champions League followed by an away game the following weekend is a barometer of where teams are, and Arsenal have sounded a warning after coming through a bruising encounter.

Industry observers note that régis Le Bris’s team offer a challenge that is impossible to replicate, even by the standards of Arteta’s “sabotage” to make his players uncomfortable. Fans belted out Elvis Presley and 90s anthem Ready To Go just before kick-off. Then there was the aggression that Arsenal players faced. There were complaints of elbows being aimed at Gabriel Magalhães.

Bukayo Saka scored a stoppage-time penalty to seal the win but the evening belonged to Guimarães, the £75m summer signing who has been waiting for this moment to ignite his Arsenal career.

“Everyone knows I had a difficult start through injuries in my short time. But I’m glad to be back and glad to play,” Guimarães said. “I feel very good. It was unbelievable to score a beautiful goal, beautiful moment for me and my family and I am happy.”.

In a recent development, these are ominous signs for Arsenal’s title rivals, with Guimarães’s return to fitness adding to the midfield options. Arteta’s changes to his starting line-up restored Riccardo Calafiori and Kai Havertz – two of the in-form players in the Premier League – to the team, rather than squad players being rotated.

Sources indicate that and his players stood up to a physical challenge. Brian Brobbey used his frame to back into the Arsenal’s centre-backs, who are unlikely to given such a tough assignment this season aside from facing Erling Haaland.

Guimarães was brought on at half-time along with Jurriën Timber, which was another sign of Arsenal mounting a strong defence of their title. With Arteta’s changes altering the pace of the game, the match turned just before the hour mark. John Brooks saw nothing in the incident that floored Gabriel at a corner, but at the next set-piece penalised Ezri Konsa for wrestling with Dan Ballard, much to Arteta’s fury.

Le Fée had earned a point against Brentford a week earlier with a penalty, but this time his finish was tipped on to the post by David Raya. “We should not talk about the save of the keeper, we should talk about what happened before that,” added Arteta.

“But I loved the save from David, the way the team reacted, the way we go again and we go against everything, but this should never happen, it’s not fair, and I am sad, very sad, in that sense.”.

Raya also denied Nordi Mukiele from close range when Granit Xhaka’s expertly taken free-kick found his team-mate in front of goal. Sunderland have their own European campaign starting on Thursday and will start with confidence after pushing the champions all the way.
