Sunderland are the latest team tasked with stopping Arsenal, who have begun their title defence in formidable style: they’ve won out of three, including a dominant comeback victory against Chelsea last weekend, and look well equipped to become the first Arsenal team to retain the title since the mid-1930s.

“I love those challenges,” noted Mikel Arteta. “I try to create them in pre-seasons so when they happen, we already experience them and we already know. So get to the stadium very late, change the routine and suddenly the players have to do something else.

We’ve done many things – made the dressing room hotter, more difficult, more challenging, less beds... because we’re going to have to adapt to different contexts.”.

So far, they’re adapting very well to the context of being the reigning champions.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JAKE FENNER, US SPORTS WRITER.

Published: 13:29 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 13:42 EST, 14 November 2026.

Perhaps it's incredibly cynical, and maybe too harsh, to call the tears that fell down the face of Mauricio Pochettino 'performative.' But it's the first word that came to mind – followed by 'surprising' and 'a bit much.'.

It was only four months ago when the Argentine who had been atop the United States' men's national team since 2024 signed a contract extension to stay on board for another four years.

'We want to try to have a lasting impact on the sport in the country that has welcomed us so warmly and for that impact to extend beyond results on the field,' Pochettino said when his contract was signed.

Yet, after a few months and one international window, that experiment to make a 'lasting impact' has ended. Pochettino may have cried because he fell in love with the country, but it's not like he got fired. Instead, he's off to lead one of the world's greatest football brands in Manchester United.

It has been revealed that so now the question turns to the legacy Pochettino leaves behind. Plenty of American soccer writers and fans point to the spirit the former Chelsea boss created and how he helped to energize a team which had been bogged down by past coaches.

It has been revealed that but Pochettino's results don't scream success. The World Cup finish was nothing special compared to his peers, his record against the best nations the USA faced was poor and he'll leave as the first full-time USMNT manager in nearly 30 years to not win at least one trophy.

Mauricio Pochettino cried as he left the United States' top job for Manchester United.

Pochettino's USMNT played exciting football, but ultimately didn't progress past the norm.

But any potential for further growth evaporated when the Argentine returned to England.

By all accounts, the greatest thing Pochettino did was install a hungry, all-in-or-nothing culture in a team bogged down by an earth-rocking scandal and a poor 2024 Copa America run.

It has been revealed that but he did so in a way that often left the biggest players of the USMNT system behind. Rather than keep a consistent core of his best players around, he seemed intent on tinkering with the lineup in each window.

According to recent reports, the results reflect that instability. Leading to the World Cup, Pochettino played 12 games against sides in the top 30 of the FIFA World Rankings. He won just three fixtures – drawing once and losing the remaining eight.

Industry observers note that all the while, he was linked to returns to Europe. Pochettino may have said in his exit press conference that he 'never said I wanted to go back to the Premier League' but the Premier League certainly wanted him – especially Tottenham.

Come World Cup time, Pochettino's team finally seemed to gel with a scintillating style of play never before seen in the USMNT.

But it all crashed down after the Round of 32 game against Bosnia when Folarin Balogun's red card was (as this American will admit) deviously overturned. The noise and controversy led to the Americans' embarrassment at the hands of Belgium on home soil.

A summer of exciting soccer for the USMNT followed years of hard resets and mixed results.

It all fell apart with a demolition by Belgium, leaving Pochettino without any success.

The Yanks were not expected to go much further than the last 16. But branding Pochettino's time atop the USMNT a 'success' on the back of this World Cup performance is giving him too much credit – especially considering the four prior managers to take the US to the World Cup all made it to that stage of the tournament as well.

With his departure confirmed, Pochettino is the first USMNT manager to leave the post without any silverware since the 1998 departure of Steve Sampson, who hadn't been a professional manager before being appointed to the job.

Even though he achieved little in terms of results, players praised Pochettino's leadership and development skills, which shouldn't be ignored.

Middlesbrough midfielder Sebastian Berhalter remarked: 'He's meant so much to me and he's helped me develop as a player and as a person. And as a player, that's all you can ask for, to have that trust and have that belief in you.'.

Recent findings suggest that but not every player in the system was tripping over themselves to play under Poch. Just ask Christian Pulisic, who took the entire summer off in 2025 to rest before the World Cup – only to put up a goose egg in his home country.

Any hope for further progress under Pochettino evaporated when United came calling.

Sources indicate that all of this being stated, there was reason for hope in the future. By re-signing Pochettino, the chance to cement that work ethic, culture and leadership presented itself.

With his extension, Pochettino had the chance to build a foundation in US Soccer to engender future success for decades to come.

It has been revealed that now, that's all gone. Now, Pochettino's time in charge will be remembered more for unfulfilled potential than culture shifting. After all, how do you expect to keep a culture if its chief architect leaves?

US Soccer now is faced with a quagmire of either hiring the biggest possible name again (Guardiola, if you believe the rumors) or hiring someone who will treat the position less like a stepping stone and more like a cornerstone.

In a recent development, it never seemed like Pochettino fully embraced the US, despite the tears on Friday. He'll be off for Old Trafford and a United squad bogged down by perpetual disappointment, all while leaving behind the biggest "What If" in the still-growing history of the American game.

Breaking: Significant Leicester City ownership upgrade emerges after being listed for £200m in August

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Leicester City have had financial problems for some time now, and discontent towards long-term owners King Power has grown amid the club’s 10-year slide from Premier League champions to League One.
  • It has been revealed that now though, after limited progress and minimal news, The Telegraph has reported that the Foxes are no longer up for sale.
  • In a recent development, despite their debt, the club were valued at £200m upon being listed for sale.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Leicester City have had financial problems for some time now, and discontent towards long-term owners King Power has grown amid the club’s 10-year slide from Premier League champions to League One. As a result of growing unrest and dire finances, LCFC were put up for sale in August.

It has been revealed that now though, after limited progress and minimal news, The Telegraph has reported that the Foxes are no longer up for sale. Senior staff in Leicestershire have been informed by the Thai leadership that the club is off the market with the full focus on winning League One promotion.

In a recent development, despite their debt, the club were valued at £200m upon being listed for sale. This valuation and the owners’ refusal to lower their asking price has proven a major stumbling block, and now there will be no takeover at the King Power Stadium.

Chairman Aiyawatt Srivaddhanaprabha was reluctant to list Leicester City for sale in the first place. He and the King Power ownership have consistently expressed a desire to lead the club back from their poor position and to their previous heights.

However, being put up for sale and entertaining takeover bids indicated that the ownership had realised they had done all they could to try and salvage the club to no avail. But, with a £200m valuation and tremendous debts, LCFC have proven a hard sell – despite their modern training ground and stature.

It means the supporters will have to stick it out with the current hierarchy for some time yet. The chairman and his close affiliate Jon Rudkin have been heavily scrutinised in recent years, but despite a shuffle in the boardroom and the appointment of James McCarron as sporting director, much of the day-to-day responsibility still lays with ‘Top’ and Rudkin.

No takeover means no new money for the Foxes. The financial hole they have dug for themselves will only get deeper.

As of the most recently published accounts, Leicester City have averaged losses of £60m per year for the past three seasons. Past accounts demonstrated their debt sat at a monstrous £163m.

Sources indicate that now, LCFC are without the Premier League riches, and revenue on the whole will decrease drastically while they stay in League One. To find some sort of salvation without a takeover, the Foxes simply have to be successful on the pitch.

An extended stint in League One will only see them burn a deeper hole in their pockets, and it will be increasingly more difficult to clamber out of it.

Declan Rice bites back at Graeme Souness: Arsenal star claims pundit doesn't understand how the game has evolved over 'old man's football' criticism - and jokes: 'My numbers aren't bad "for a centre-back!"'

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (555 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 15:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 15:40 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Declan Rice has laughed off criticism from Graeme Souness by claiming his numbers 'aren't bad for a centre back', after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' and 'cheating' by dropping into defence.
  • Souness has long believed the Arsenal and England star does not do enough for a midfielder and mentioned recently he might as well play centre back, adding that he would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 15:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 15:40 EST, 14 November 2026.

Declan Rice has laughed off criticism from Graeme Souness by claiming his numbers 'aren't bad for a centre back', after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' and 'cheating' by dropping into defence.

Souness has long believed the Arsenal and England star does not do enough for a midfielder and mentioned recently he might as well play centre back, adding that he would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

Rice is aware of what Souness has said but believes his return of 22 goals and 33 assists since joining the Gunners in 2023 disproves the former Liverpool midfielder's opinion.

It has been revealed that ‘My numbers since I joined Arsenal speak for themselves,’ mentioned Rice. ‘For a “centre back”, I think that’s not bad numbers. I’ve had a lot of assists, a lot of goals. To be a top-class centre back getting those numbers, I’m delighted with that!’.

Recent findings suggest that rice, who will start as an advanced midfielder when England take on Spain here in Madrid on Sunday night, added: ‘Look, Graeme’s got his opinion. I think he’s had his opinion since my West Ham days. I’ve seen his views. I can’t change his opinion. I can only do what I do, which is go on the pitch, perform, play well and block out the noise.’.

Rice also believes Souness, 73, may not understand how the game has evolved.

England and Arsenal midfielder Declan Rice has laughed off Graeme Souness' criticism after he was accused of playing 'old man's football' 'cheating' by dropping into defence.

Pundit Souness believes Rice would not get a game for the likes of Real Madrid and Barcelona.

‘If you speak about the positioning, the “old man's football”, look at Harry Kane, for instance,’ began Rice. 'We played him the other week and he dropped next to the centre backs 20-30 times to pick up the ball. The game is different now. It's what the game demands, to get away from your man, to go into different areas to create overloads, to create two v ones, to progress the ball up the pitch. Football is way different. It's changed a lot, and you're always trying to look for tactical advantages.

Industry observers note that ‘In terms of me as a midfielder, I'm constantly watching clips with Mikel (Arteta). He's constantly coaching me on the pitch. How I can progress the ball from deep, drop next to the goalkeeper, go to full back to get on the ball, to take the ball up the pitch.

‘So, I feel like we're now seeing something totally different to what he would see, but in his time football was different. He was a top-class midfielder who won lots of stuff. There's no argument against him. As a pundit, as a person, his career, you have to respect what he's done.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I didn't get to see him play, but obviously his accolades were top, and I've never got to meet him in person. If I did, there would be no disrespect. I’d shake his hand. I’d chat with him. It’s an opinion at the end of the day. It’s football.’.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Lewis Nolan | 18 Nov 2026 00:11.
  • JJ Gabriel has posted a farewell message to Manchester United fans ahead of his impending switch to Real Madrid.
  • Mauricio Pochettino has not taken charge of a single training session as head coach of the club, but one of his first tasks will be to deal with the fallout of a damaging exit.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Nolan | 18 Nov 2026 00:11.

JJ Gabriel has posted a farewell message to Manchester United fans ahead of his impending switch to Real Madrid.

Mauricio Pochettino has not taken charge of a single training session as head coach of the club, but one of his first tasks will be to deal with the fallout of a damaging exit.

Teenager Gabriel revealed in September that he wished to move away from Old Trafford, and while he was registered with the club until the end of the season, that would not prevent him from moving to a club in the European Union once he turned 16.

A number of sides were reported to be interested in signing him, but Real Madrid have seemingly won the race for his signature.

Gabriel has confirmed his exit from United in a farewell video message posted to his Instagram page on Tuesday.

??? JJ Gabriel: “Goodbye and thank you, Man United”. https://t.co/5uXeBLHIcX.

Though there have been many reasons to be critical of United's approach to their young stars, it would be harsh to reprimand them over losing Gabriel.

It was reported earlier this year that the teenager and his entourage were disappointed about the pathway into first-team football, but the youngster only turned 16 on October 6.

Perhaps Gabriel believed he should have been fast-tracked into the XI like Lamine Yamal was at Barcelona and Spain, but the Baca winger's progression into senior football was anomalous.

It should also be noted that he will have to battle against the likes of Kylian Mbappe, Vinicius Junior, Arda Guler, Endrick and Yan Diomande for a place in Real Madrid's team, so it remains to be seen if he is given the minutes he desires.

Though United have not necessarily conducted themselves poorly in regard to Gabriel's exit, the saga may have an unfortunate impact on their image as a fruitful hub for young talent.

United are currently engulfed in a relegation battle in the Premier League, and the atmosphere at Old Trafford has arguably never been more toxic.

The failures of the team on the pitch and the chaos behind the scenes may deter younger talents from joining United in the future, though the club's hierarchy will hope that Pochettino can restore the club's place as a premier destination.

Tech Report: Gila explains how he went from ‘rock bottom’ at Lazio to joining Milan: “More kindness”

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (603 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Sempremilan

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.
  • Recent findings suggest that gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services.
  • Recent findings suggest that the following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Mario Gila has explained how he managed to get through a difficult time at the start of his Italy adventure, eventually performing at such a high level that AC Milan decided to sign him.

Recent findings suggest that gila left Real Madrid and Spain in the summer of 2022, when he was just 21 years old, as Lazio secured his services. In his first season, however, he only got 765 minutes on the pitch and didn’t play a single game in the second half of the campaign.

Recent findings suggest that the following season, it was as if things had changed completely, as the centre-back started performing really well and was rewarded with a lot of playing time. The growth only continued from there, resulting in Milan paying good money for him in the summer.

In his long interview with AC Milan for the interview series The Chamber, Gila discussed his initial struggles in Italy, hitting ‘rock bottom’ in his first season with Lazio. A psychologist and a changed mindset helped him get through it all.

Industry observers note that when you make a mistake, are you very demanding and hard on yourself? I mean, how do you treat yourself when something doesn’t go the way you wanted?

Industry observers note that “In the past, for example… I’ve changed a great deal. I went through a really difficult time early in my career here in Italy and hit rock bottom, but with outside help, psychological support, I got through it.

Recent findings suggest that “That’s why I keep saying ‘before’. Back then, I was very hard on myself. I didn’t allow myself to fail. If I did, I was extremely negative towards myself, I couldn’t accept that I might fail or make mistakes.

“Now I handle it much better. Now I feel that making mistakes is part of the job, it’s something that helps you improve, something that helps you grow. So I deal with it much more calmly, I process it much better internally.

“I think you still need to hold yourself to high standards and you also need to know how to find a solution to that mistake, whether in your career or in your personal life, but with much more calm and more kindness towards myself.”.

Regarding that difficult period you went through, which helped you grow and taught you so many things, you mentioned therapy. Could you tell me, not so much what happened, but what your experience with therapy was like? I mean, what did it give you at first?

It has been revealed that “I sought help from a psychologist because I was going through a very difficult time and couldn’t find a way to move forward. We’re expected to deal with situations… that I find mentally overwhelming, at just 21 years old, when you have no professional experience, because in the end, everything comes at you so fast.

“So I went to a psychologist, and completely changed my perspective. I mean, I started seeing everything negative that happened to me as a step forward, thinking: this is something that will help you improve, something you needed to go through.

“Everything changed when I changed my perspective. I used to be very hard on myself, very hard, I demanded so much of myself. Now I’m someone who feels much more at ease.

“We can all fail, make mistakes, go through difficult situations, So the way I treat myself, the way I respond to myself, the way I talk to myself, I think it plays a crucial role in maintaining a consistently positive mindset.”.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • West Ham goalkeeper Mads Hermansen has been under fire recently, with poor performances prompting calls for Alphonse Areola to be brought into the starting XI.
  • And, after the international break, doubts remain over Areola’s availability.
  • Elsewhere, Max Kilman is suspended, but Kyle Walker-Peters could be in line for a return.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

West Ham goalkeeper Mads Hermansen has been under fire recently, with poor performances prompting calls for Alphonse Areola to be brought into the starting XI. However, the Frenchman suffered an injury in the warm-up before WHUFC’s defeat to Blackburn Rovers before the break, ruling him out.

And, after the international break, doubts remain over Areola’s availability. Speaking to the official club media ahead of Saturday’s clash with Preston North End, Scott Parker said: “We’re struggling a bit with Alphonse at the moment. He probably looks a bit unlikely. We’ll probably leave it as late as we can to see if he’s fit to be involved.”.

Elsewhere, Max Kilman is suspended, but Kyle Walker-Peters could be in line for a return. Parker made no mention of the full-back in his pre-match interview, saying: “There’s nothing really jumping out, other than Alphonse.”.

Areola isn’t ruled out of West Ham’s clash with Preston North End, but it would be a surprise to see him start. If Parker goes into the weekend planning to start the Frenchman and it transpires that he isn’t ready to go on matchday, it throws that section of the pre-match preparations out of the window.

It has been revealed that despite his struggle for form, it is smarter to prepare for the game with Hermansen in goal. That will frustrate some sections of the WHUFC support, but it is the sensible move to make.

Hermansen has started every Championship game this season, but his performances have been far from convincing.

It has been revealed that he isn’t solely responsible for the underwhelming defensive record of four clean sheets and 24 goals conceded in 16 games across all competitions. However, the Dane’s displays have left a lot to be desired with an inability to command his box and errors when coming to claim crosses leading to chances for the opposition.

Sources indicate that given his form, a fully fit Areola may have got the nod. For this weekend though, it seems Hermansen will keep his place.

When Areola is at 100%, Hermansen will have a fight on his hands to keep his place.

It means that if he does start again against Preston North End as expected, he needs to put in a far more assured performance. A clean sheet would not go amiss, but the most important thing is to act with confidence and conviction. If he can command his box, comfortably claim crosses and show composure on the ball, it will go a long way to easing concerns around his form.

In a recent development, if not, Areola will be waiting in the wings to come into the WHUFC side when fit. If his absence extends longer, then youngster Finlay Herrick may be considered if Parker feels a chance is needed.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Published: 16:25 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 16:42 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.
  • FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been sanctioned after a horrifying foul with Tenerife's De Miguel earlier this month.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Published: 16:25 EST, 13 November 2026 | Updated: 16:42 EST, 14 November 2026.

The goalkeeper involved in the collision that killed Spanish footballer Jesus de Miguel has been hit with a 12-match ban - but may never play again.

FC Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been sanctioned after a horrifying foul with Tenerife's De Miguel earlier this month.

Owono was sent off and the match was abandoned with De Miguel, 30, admitted to intensive care, where he later died.

The goalkeeper was subjected to chants of 'murderer' by Tenerife supporters and retreated from public view amid the significant backlash.

Now his manager Carles Manso has noted: 'We will ​give him space so that he feels completely free to make ‌any ⁠decision, whether he wants to return, when, or if he does not want to return.

'When he feels it is appropriate and when ​he feels genuinely ready to take a ​decision ⁠like that [he will do so].

Andorra goalkeeper Jesus Owono has been banned for 12 games and could quit football for good after he collided with Tenerife's Jesus De Miguel, who died.

The striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as the keeper attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

De Miguel was rushed to hospital following the incident after appearing motionless on the pitch.

'What we have to do is support him in every way and be close to ​him.'.

Earlier this month, Owono issued a statement describing his 'enormous pain' following the tragic on-field collision.

It has been revealed that owono said: 'These are being the most difficult days of my life. I am struggling to find the words and find it very difficult to assimilate anything that has happened.

Recent findings suggest that 'I feel an enormous pain for the loss of Jesús. I think of him, his family, and everyone who loved him. I know there will be many issues to address; I will face whatever comes with the utmost respect.

According to recent reports, 'But right now, honestly, I cannot think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing. Rest in peace, Jesus.'.

The tragedy occurred as the game entered the seventh minute of stoppage time, when De Miguel looked set to race away on the counter-attack for Tenerife in search of a winner.

As he watched a long ball drop into his path, the striker was struck in the chest by Owono's flying knee as he attempted to clear the ball near the halfway line.

After initially rolling around on the floor, De Miguel became motionless, and medical staff rushed onto the pitch to attend to him.

Police are investigating the death of De Miguel due to protocol, and they are also now probing the emergency medical response.

Owono said he could not 'think of anything else except Jesús and the pain we are experiencing' (Source: Instagram/Jesus Owono).

Tenerife striker De Miguel died in the morning following the horrifying clash with Owono.

Owono was initially given a red card for the challenge before the decision was soon taken by the referee to abandon the fixture.

De Miguel was seen to for over five minutes while his team-mates were visibly distressed, with some appearing to be in tears.

The stadium had been in complete silence while De Miguel was being treated, but as he was taken off the pitch the striker was given a standing ovation by the crowd.

He had become a father just last year, and according to El Espanol, his wife and baby daughter were watching in the stands as the fatal incident occurred.

After being taken to an ambulance on a stretcher, there is believed to have been an approximate 15-minute wait before they made their way to the hospital.

De Miguel is believed to have suffered a cardiac arrest while being transported to hospital and had to be revived inside the ambulance, according to Spanish media outlet Marca.

Spanish newspaper AS reported that De Miguel's team-mates had travelled to hospital after he had been taken to intensive care.

In a statement, CD Tenerife confirmed the striker's death, saying: 'Broken with pain, with a lump in our throat and unable to believe that this is true, from CD Tenerife we communicate the tragic death, this Tuesday, November 3, 2026, at 8:00 a.m., of Jesus de Miguel Alameda.'.

Tenerife stated: 'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome'.

'There are no words of comfort; there is absolutely nothing to mitigate this feeling full of sadness.

'We are with his devastated family, with his loved ones, with all the people of Tenerife who today mourn this cruel outcome.

'The family of Jesus de Miguel is grateful for each and every one of the expressions of support received, and also requests, from the bottom of its heart, maximum respect for his privacy, in these terrible moments.'.

Troyes vs Le Havre - prediction, team news, lineups

💡 Key Takeaways
  • By Joel Lefevre | 18 Nov 2026 02:01.
  • The bottom two teams in Ligue 1 will kick off matchday 11 of the campaign Friday as Troyes welcome Le Havre to Stade de l’Aube.
  • Heading into this match, Troyes are 17th in the table after suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain, putting them six points above the Normandy club, who lost their last league fixture 2-0 at home to Lorient.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Joel Lefevre | 18 Nov 2026 02:01.

The bottom two teams in Ligue 1 will kick off matchday 11 of the campaign Friday as Troyes welcome Le Havre to Stade de l’Aube.

Heading into this match, Troyes are 17th in the table after suffering a narrow 1-0 defeat at Paris Saint-Germain, putting them six points above the Normandy club, who lost their last league fixture 2-0 at home to Lorient.

Some improved results of late have brought Troyes back within reach of Ligue 1 safety after 10 matchdays in the top flight.

After losing five successive matches in this competition, Stephane Dumont has seen his side earn points in two of their last three contests.

One of the biggest improvements has been their poise at the back, as they have collected two clean sheets in their last three league fixtures after conceding multiple goals in five straight games.

While their defensive game is much improved, they are still struggling to create many scoring opportunities, sitting dead last in the league for big chances so far.

On Friday, they can claim consecutive Ligue 1 triumphs at Stade de l’Aube for the first time since March-April 2022, after beating Le Mans on Halloween (2-0).

ESTAC have won three of their last four home meetings with Le Havre, all in Ligue 2, and have lost just one of their last five games against them.

It is an urgent time for Le Havre, who enter this matchday six points back of Ligue 1 safety and are the only side yet to win this season.

The club have said that this is an emergency situation and, as such, appointed Valerien Ismael as the upcoming manager in hopes of getting out of the relegation zone.

The well-travelled coach, who was born in Strasbourg, has a reputation for turning clubs around promptly, taking Barnsley from a team near the bottom of the Championship to a playoff position by the end of the 2020-21 campaign.

Ismael has a big job ahead of him, to transform a side in Le Havre, who have given up the joint-second-most goals in Ligue 1 thus far (22).

He takes over a team that have suffered six consecutive defeats in this competition, while earning just one point away from home this season.

While they have not fared well against Troyes of late, Le Ciel et Marine are unbeaten against them in Ligue 1 this century, winning that last meeting in Normandy in 2003 (1-0).

Due to an ankle injury, Troyes are expected to be without Anis Ouzenadji on Friday, and Yacouba Kone is dealing with a sore knee.

From matchday nine to 10, we saw two fresh faces in their starting 11, with Ismael Boura and Kandet Diawara replacing Paolo Gozzi and Timothe Nkada, while Hillel Konate got the start between the sticks yet again.

As for Le Havre, Rassoul Ndiaye and Elias Jelert are doubtful because of leg injuries, while Timothee Pembele is dealing with adductor pain and unlikely to feature.

Lionel Mpasi and Felix Mambimbi are out with Achilles tendon ruptures, while Stephan Zagadou is recovering from a cruciate ligament tear.

Troyes possible starting lineup:.

Konate; Maronnier, Monfray, Diaz, Boura; Mille, Karim, Diop; Le Douaron, Ripart, Nkada.

Le Havre possible starting lineup:.

Bodart; Sasso, Koffi, Touba; Ouziad, Ebonog, Mwanga, Richardson; Fofana, Samatta; Maja.

Ismael has a reputation for elevating his teams promptly, and against a Troyes side that are not terribly potent in front of goal, we believe the Normandy club will catch a break and pull out a narrow victory.

Liverpool want to sign Athletic Club midfielder Mikel Jauregizar, who is seen as an alternative to Lamine Camara, the newest report has claimed.

The Merseysiders are preparing to take on rivals Manchester United on Sunday, and victory will be key for the club's pursuit of a place in Premier League's top four.

If Andoni Iraola's side are to get the better of the Red Devils, they will need to win the midfield battle, though that has been an area of concern for some time.

Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai have often disappointed in the middle of the pitch, and that has led to calls for reinforcements.

While Liverpool have strongly been credited interest in Monaco star Camara, Anfield Watch have now claimed that the Reds also have Athletic Bilbao's Jauregizar on their list of targets.

Valued at just under £21m by Transfermarkt, Jauregizar would likely not command as high a fee as Camara, which would make a January move more realistic.

The 23-year-old has only started three La Liga games this season, featuring in seven, and he has won 51% of his duels in the top flight.

Jauregizar only won 47% of his duels in the league in 2025-26, but his struggles in that regard are not shared with Camara, who has won 66% of his duels this campaign in Ligue 1.

The Monaco midfielder is also more accomplished with the ball, and he should still be seen as the premium option, either in January or the summer.

Trey Nyoni will almost certainly become a starter in the next few years, and signing another midfielder would pose a problem in terms of guaranteeing playing time.

Szoboszlai and Gravenberch are contracted to Anfield until 2031 and 2032 respectively, so moving on either player would be difficult.

Alexis Mac Allister has been the Reds' best midfielder this season and has arguably been among the best performers in that role across the division, so losing him in the coming summer would weaken the squad.

Liverpool may soon be faced with a painful decision, with at least one of their established stars likely to head for the exit doors in the coming months.

Sheffield Wednesday are back in action on Friday as they face Yorkshire rivals Barnsley at Oakwell. Dave Challinor will be eager to build on his first SWFC win against Plymouth Argyle, and he’ll be helped by an improving injury picture at Hillsborough.

Recent findings suggest that speaking to the press ahead of Friday’s game, Challinor revealed that star forward Louie Barry is fit for the clash with the Tykes after making his return off the bench against Plymouth. The 23-year-old has come through another week of training scot-free, but the boss remains wary that he needs to be managed carefully after his long-term ankle injury.

Elsewhere, Ashley Maynard-Brewer and Ali Al-Hamadi have trained with no challenges, and internationals Kieran Morrison, Jordi Liongola, Sean Fusire and Will Grainger returned with no injuries. With no upcoming blows, the Owls only remain without Max Lowe, Reece James, Mason Burstow and Tyler Onyango.

Sheffield Wednesday have lacked a killer instinct in attack at times this season. The failure to convert control into goals played a part in Henrik Pedersen’s downfall, so it is down to Challinor to right the ship.

The 3-0 win over Plymouth Argyle showed big attacking improvements, and their frontline only grows stronger with Barry’s return. He is a proven star at League One level and has already shown SWFC fans how potent he can be in his limited time on the pitch since joining in the summer.

Barry’s comeback will give Challinor a welcome but tricky selection dilemma to resolve. The former Aston Villa and Barcelona prospect can play at striker or on the left-hand side, and there is strong competition for both of these positions.

Davis Keillor-Dunn‘s form has seen him solidify a place in the team, while it was Callum Slattery and Barry Bannan who played in the most advanced roles behind the number nine against Plymouth Argyle.

In a recent development, if Challinor is to play with a three-man frontline, Barry may be perfect for the place on the left. However, the Owls boss will have to work out who drops from the team to facilitate his inclusion.

According to recent reports, there is an understandable eagerness to see Barry back in the first XI. He is one of League One’s standout players and has the potential to be a real star in an exciting chapter at Sheffield Wednesday.

According to recent reports, however, Challinor is right in saying that he can only play such a role if they are smart with his return. If they rush him into too much too soon, he will be at risk of re-injury or separate setbacks.

By managing his minutes over the coming weeks, SWFC give themselves the best chance of having Barry fit and available for longer. He will be a key influence in Challinor’s attack, but only if they’re careful in the early days of his comeback.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Arsenal could face imminent disappointment in their pursuit of AFC Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, with David Ornstein providing an enhancement on the 19-year-old's future.
  • The Gunners have been monitoring the Frenchman after his impressive performances, but a move for him in the January transfer window is now looking increasingly unlikely.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 06:57.

Arsenal could face imminent disappointment in their pursuit of AFC Bournemouth forward Eli Junior Kroupi, with David Ornstein providing an enhancement on the 19-year-old's future.

The Gunners have been monitoring the Frenchman after his impressive performances, but a move for him in the January transfer window is now looking increasingly unlikely.

Ornstein has also suggested that Kroupi could favour a move away from the Premier League when he eventually leaves the Vitality Stadium.

In a recent The Athletic Q&A, Ornstein downplayed the prospect of the Cherries sanctioning a January departure, saying the club has little financial incentive to sell midway through the campaign.

The forward is under contract until 2030, meaning the Cherries are in a strong negotiating position and can afford to wait until the summer before considering significant offers.

Ornstein also highlighted that Kroupi only made his first appearance of the season on October 25th after an injury lay-off, with Bournemouth keen to benefit from his contributions during the remainder of the campaign.

Perhaps more significantly for Arsenal, the ever-reliable journalist suggested that the teenager could prefer a move abroad rather than another Premier League club.

Paris Saint-Germain and Barcelona have both been heavily linked, with Ornstein indicating that the information available to him points towards those destinations being more likely than a move within England.

He did acknowledge that an exceptional financial offer from a Premier League club could change the situation, but his expectation is that Bournemouth would be more receptive to a sale next summer.

Ornstein's upgrade represents a significant complication for Arsenal, who could now need to explore alternative attacking targets if they want to strengthen in January.

Kroupi's contract situation means Bournemouth have little reason to entertain offers, while the player's reported preference for moving abroad further weakens the Gunners' position.

Antonio Nusa could therefore become a more realistic alternative for Gunners boss Mikel Arteta.

The RB Leipzig winger is another young attacking talent attracting Premier League interest, with Arsenal previously linked alongside Tottenham and reportedly confident of competing for his signature.

Nusa would not necessarily provide the same centre-forward option as Kroupi, but his ability to operate out wide could address another area where Arsenal need greater depth.

Ultimately, Kroupi remains an exciting long-term target, but the combination of Bournemouth's stance and his apparent preference for a move abroad suggests Arsenal may have to be patient or turn their attention elsewhere in January.

Woeful Man Utd have no excuses, Carrick is under big pressure

📅 13 Sep 2026 | ⏱️ 31 min read (6210 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~31 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United.
  • They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.
  • Sources indicate that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This was a kick in the midriff for Manchester United. Not once. But twice. And, then, most painfully, a third time with a dismal, dispiriting defeat.

They profited from the first one with Phil Foden sent off after hitting out at Bruno Fernandes – in retaliation – after he was booted in the backside by the United captain who somehow went unpunished.

Sources indicate that but then City played three quarters of this 199th Manchester derby with just 10 men and came out on top with the inevitable and outstanding Erling Haaland scoring his ninth goal against United to become the top scorer in Premier League meetings between these rivals. And that was a far more painful and damaging blow.

Erling Haaland has put Manchester City ahead in the derby after a VAR check ⚽️ pic.twitter.com/V0DCwryhFy.

On a day in which thousands of fans protested, accusing co-owners Sir Jim Ratcliffe and the Glazers – with Avram Glazer joining Ratcliffe in attendance – of treating them like “s---”, United unfortunately left a nasty whiff of being just that out on the pitch.

Sources indicate that united were frankly, woeful. They lacked belief and imagination and attacking instinct and too many of their players – their apparent big players – went missing when they needed to stand up and take the game by the scruff of the neck. They could not break down City’s defence and failed to be a front-foot team who can dominate the ball. Which is surely what they aspire to be?

Sources indicate that they hit the post twice – through Marcus Rashford and Kobbie Mainoo – with efforts from 25 yards. And those two local lads were by far their best players. Without them, United carried so little threat, were so blunt, that it was shocking.

It has been revealed that the question for Michael Carrick, the Manchester United head coach, is simple: what is he trying to do with this team? Can they only ever depend on counter-attacks?

Afterwards Haaland talked about City’s “personality, character” and that was exactly what United lacked. They did not adapt a tactical proposal to combat 10-man City’s desire to keep their wingers high and wide, and break with intent and still try and attack.

According to recent reports, it was telling that so little did City’s latest head coach Enzo Maresca worry about United that he did not add a defensive player, and when he took off Rayan Cherki at half-time, he replaced him with the equally creative Iliman Ndiaye who impressed. Maresca knew United needed space to run in behind and denied them that. It was that simple.

City also struck the post with United goalkeeper Senne Lammens tipping an Enzo Fernández shot against the frame of the goal, and the visitors were worthy winners as they preserved their perfect start to the season to draw level on points with leaders, Arsenal.

City handled the occasion and the – admittedly toothless – opposition superbly under their fresh head coach and will clearly be Arsenal’s closest challengers this season.

According to recent reports, maresca delivered a masterclass. For Carrick? This was a disasterclass. An object lesson in how not to use a man-advantage. And now United will have to endure even more City songs after being outplayed at home like this.

Sources indicate that was it complacency? Was it inability? Was it a damning lack of courage, confidence, belief even? On the pitch and in the dugout United were far too passive. This was not how a massive team plays and Carrick needs to wake up.

The former midfielder did so well last season to guide United into Champions League qualification but so far this campaign he has given the impression that his job is done. Rather than that the real work starts now.

Recent findings suggest that there was controversy around the red card and the goal. There is no doubt Foden had to go. But what about Fernandes? He clearly kicked Foden as he was on the ground with the midfielder reacting instinctively, two-footing him in the gut.

It meant he became the first City player to be dismissed in a Manchester derby in the league since Bernardo Corradi in December 2006 and will be punished with a three-match ban for violent conduct.

To make matters worse for Foden, who missed out on the World Cup, it happened in front of Thomas Tuchel who names his England squad for the Nations League campaign on Friday.

Phil Foden is SENT OFF in the Manchester derby! 🟥 pic.twitter.com/sDkHoLMnjL.

Sources indicate that and the goal? Initially it was ruled out for offside as Haaland superbly turned in Josko Gvardiol’s cross beyond the far post – he made that tricky finish look routine. But after a lengthy VAR check that decision was overturned by referee Michael Oliver.

Industry observers note that patrick Dorgu had played Haaland onside but the problem then was whether Fernández had touched the ball as he tried to reach the cross. He had not. But even if he had not, surely he was impeding Lisandro Martínez’s attempt to clear? He was certainly in the defender’s line of vision which fits the criteria for the offside to be given as it interfered with an opponent.

It has been revealed that united can understandably complain but they can have no excuse. The pressure, already, will be beginning to mount on Carrick with just four points from four league games and down in 13th place. With a Carabao Cup tie at home to Brighton in midweek and a trip to Fulham next Sunday before the international break, he needs wins.

Recent findings suggest that “We’ve only got 10 men,” goaded the City fans as the game headed into added time and United can expect to hear that again and again. And again.

Even so, at the death, Bryan Mbeumo – as otherwise anonymous as Matheus Cunha – had the chance to equalise after being shrewdly picked out by Fernandes. He was excellently thwarted by Gianluigi Donnarumma. But Mbeumo was clear inside the penalty area and had to score. Not that United would have deserved it. There were boos at the end and understandably so. United were just not good enough.

Recent findings suggest that I’m confused. We put things in place in the game now. We have people in offices with all the screens for this decision. It’s more worrying about if that’s the interpretation of football now. If that’s the interpretation of not interfering in the game now, that’s really worrying for me. It’s a staggering explanation.

Industry observers note that the decision isn’t going to change the season, but it’s had a major impact on the game. That decision wasn’t on us today. It’s up to us to create and score after that. We had moments. Of course it’s up to us to do that, but significant moments in games like that have a big impact.

In a recent development, we did a lot of things well, it looked like we were growing well into the game. We looked dangerous. We’ll take the positives from the game today and move on well, but we’re not moving on lightly.

According to recent reports, we could have created more. That’s an answer for us, but we could have. That’s our second defeat now, since I’ve been in charge, but we’re a good team and we’ll get back to wining ways.

The red card changed the plan of the game but credit to the players because the effort, spirit and togetherness has been brilliant.

Industry observers note that [On Foden’s red card] Can be a red card, but in the same action can be a red card for Bruno. It is what it is, we won.

In a recent development, changed the proposal for us, and changed the plan for them. They are unbelievable in transition, and the moment we are with 10 men we give them no transitions.

When you are able to win a game with 10 players it’s fantastic, when this game is a derby it’s even better.

Last year with Chelsea I had a player sent off here after three minutes, this year 25, hopefully next time we play against 11vs11!

Recent findings suggest that both of these teams were in Champions League action this week but, as James Ducker explores in this piece, United have missed out in six of the last 13 campaigns. City have been ever-presents, with significant sporting and financial benefits. Over the 10 years between 2016 and 2025, City generated £343m more in broadcast revenue and prize money from European football than their derby rivals.

Industry observers note that sam Wallace was at Carrington this week to speak with Diogo Dalot, the Manchester United right-back who could make his 250th appearance for the club this afternoon. Dalot has been through some tumultuous times at Old Trafford, and is one of the great survivors in the squad. He talks about the scrutiny at United, his musical family and the negatives of social media for young players in an interview you can read here.

My sense is that while United fans generally understand and agree with the decision to stick with Carrick, they hope he is the long-term answer to get the club back to winning the Premier League or Champions League, while the rest of the world doubts it.

Recent findings suggest that to most, it feels like Carrick remains an interim solution in all but name, entrusted with the keys to Old Trafford until a super coach can move in during the summer of 2027. Carrick will not see it that way, of course, but there are certain perceptions which will be tough to shake off.

Good afternoon and welcome to our live coverage of the season’s first Manchester derby, with midfield rebuilds the theme of the summer on both sides of town.

Elliot Anderson, Enzo Fernandez and Ayyoub Bouaddi could all be involved for City, who lost Rodri and Bernardo Silva in the engine room, while United have recruited Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos in an attempt to address a long-standing problem.

Recent findings suggest that rodri’s departure and a Community Shield shellacking by Arsenal prompted some gloomy forecasts for Enzo Maresca and City, but confidence has grown since. The late turnaround at home to Bournemouth on the opening weekend could well look very vital in a few months’ time, while Crystal Palace and Coventry have also been put away. Victory in Porto was probably Maresca’s most impressive result to date at City, though winning at Old Trafford would usurp that. Three points for City would mean they join Arsenal on a maximum of 12 points from four games.

Sources indicate that it has been a patchy start to the campaign for United and Michael Carrick, and this afternoon’s result will go a long way to shaping perceptions of where they are. The concession of a late equalise at Everton, in addition to a dreadful loss at Hull, adds a degree of pressure. United will be buoyed by their performance in this fixture in January, when they delivered possibly the best performance of the post-Ferguson years to slay City in a 2-0 win that could well have been four or five.

With Tielemans, Bruno Fernandes and Kobbie Mainoo prominent in midfield, United are trying to shift to a more possession-heavy approach, but any success against City in recent times has tended to come on the counter-attack. Maresca’s team have had lots of the ball in their first few games of the season, so that is the expected pattern again.Full team news on the way later.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By OLIVER HOLT, CHIEF SPORTS WRITER and CRAIG HOPE, CHIEF FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 16:03 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 16:48 EST, 14 November 2026.

Thomas Tuchel was dragged into a bitter race row on the eve of England's Nations League showdown with Spain.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols in case their players suffered racist abuse at the Metropolitano Stadium on Sunday evening.

England players were notoriously subject to racial abuse at the Bernabeu in 2004 and England have not played in Madrid since.

But Spain manager Luis de la Fuente reacted angrily when he was told that Tuchel had addressed the subject.

Sources indicate that 'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente said. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'.

The row then deepened when a Spanish journalist told Tuchel about De La Fuente's reaction and the England coach grew exasperated with the line of questioning.

Tuchel had been asked before England's departure for Spain about England's protocols.

'Tell Tuchel that there is no racism in Spain,' de la Fuente said. 'Just like in England. We are not racist.'.

'I was polite enough to answer a question from your colleagues,' Tuchel said, 'and you run and ask Spain's coach and tell them that I talked about racism in Spain.

Recent findings suggest that 'I never talked about racism in Spain. I answered a question politely. I never expect racism. The dressing room is the most anti-racist place in the world. This is a perfect example of how you create confusion out of nothing.'.

In a recent development, tuchel had earlier said: 'It's vital that the players know about the protocol. And then, yeah, we will give our answers if stuff like this happens. Best answers are on the pitch.

It has been revealed that 'We had a same discussion before the Serbia game [in Belgrade in September 2025]. There is a protocol in place.'.

England midfielder Declan Rice stated that Tuchel had not yet addressed the group about racism protocols but that they were clear about what they would do if any England players were abused.

England's game against Bulgaria in Sofia in 2019 was halted after allegations of racism against England players but the game was completed.

Thomas Tuchel has revealed that James Trafford will face world champions Spain on Sunday night, raising questions over Jordan Pickford’s status as England’s No 1.

It was assumed that Pickford, who the head coach maintains is his first choice, would keep the jersey given the identity of the opposition and the chance for England to top their Nations League group with victory here in Madrid.

However, Tuchel will hand Leeds stopper Trafford his fifth cap at the Metropolitano Stadium.

Recent findings suggest that ’We want to try and see how far Traff is,’ remarked Tuchel, who rotated his keepers during last month’s international break. ‘So he gets a highly competitive match. We had some changes in the back four in the last match (2-1 win over Croatia on Thursday), so we went for more stability and more experience with Pickers.

‘Tomorrow is a high-pressure match, on the biggest stage, and it's exactly what we need to see where we are with him (Trafford). Hopefully he's not too over-excited or overly nervous, because there's no need to be. We trust him. But it is different to play for England than to play for your club.

'To have the opportunity to play matches where it really matters is the best way to show up, and to show that you're ready.’.

It was put to Tuchel that it would make more sense to play the goalkeeper he believes is his No 1 in the biggest game from this round of fixtures.

It has been revealed that ’It was the circumstances of the last match, that we had some changes in the back four, and that was the decision in the goalkeeping team,’ he said. 'Jordan is at the moment our No.1. I have a very clear picture in high-pressure moments. He played in tournaments and played for me in the World Cup.’.

Meanwhile, centre back Ezri Konsa is also set to start after recovering from a knee problem.

In a recent development, ‘I’m very pleased with how he has fitted in seamlessly at Arsenal,’ said Tuchel. ‘It just looks like he's always been there. For us, it’s amazing that he plays on the highest level, competes for every title, is in an atmosphere and in a situation where it really matters that you stay focused and you show up every three days. It's only positives for us.’.

PROBABLE ENGLAND XI: Trafford; White, Quansah, Konsa, Hall; Anderson, Rice; Rogers, Jude Bellingham, Gordon; Kane.

  • Sources indicate that while the January transfer window is yet to open, Liverpool are facing a dilemma behind the scenes.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Axel Clody | 18 Nov 2026 07:04.

Liverpool have reportedly entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem, with the future of Virgil van Dijk still unresolved. The Dutch defender’s contract runs until the end of the season and he has yet to reach an agreement over an extension, while Liverpool are monitoring the market.

Sources indicate that while the January transfer window is yet to open, Liverpool are facing a dilemma behind the scenes. With his contract running until the end of the season, Van Dijk has no renewal agreement in progress and can sign a pre-contract agreement from January.

With the situation of the Dutch defender unresolved, Liverpool have entered the race with Barcelona to sign a Brazilian gem.

According to Sports Illustrated, Liverpool have sent scouts to follow the rise of Arthur Dias closely and are now assessing the possibility of buying him from Athletico Paranaense. The 19-year-old defender is one of the breakout stars of Brazilian football in 2026 and is being watched by several European clubs.

Barcelona’s interest in Arthur Dias is long-standing, as being left-footed and comfortable playing out from the back are qualities missing from manager Hansi Flick’s squad. Van Dijk, who is right-footed but also plays on the left side of central defence, would leave a gap for Liverpool to fill should he depart.

The Brazilian centre-back has a contract until December 2028 and has already seen a Tottenham Hotspur offer of £18m (€21m) rejected by Athletico Paranaense. The club’s board believes Arthur Dias should only be released for an offer of at least £25.5m (€30m) because of his high potential.

So far, Liverpool have made no formal approach to Athletico Paranaense for the young defender, but the competition is not limited to Barcelona.

Clubs such as Bayer Leverkusen and RB Leipzig are also monitoring Arthur Dias, who gained international visibility with his first two call-ups to the Brazil national team in the post-World Cup international breaks.

Industry observers note that brazilian aside, Liverpool’s number four has no guaranteed future at Anfield. Despite his idol status and undisputed place in the starting line-up under manager Andoni Iraola, Van Dijk has no advanced talks with the club’s directors over his stay, with moves towards an extension expected to gather pace at the turn of the year.

The captain himself admitted in a recent interview that he plans to stay at Liverpool, but has no news on his situation.

The Spanish manager is in favour of Van Dijk staying, as the Dutchman is not only a leadership figure in the dressing room but also a pillar of the defensive system, having won 75% of his duels in this season’s Premier League.

In that context, AC Milan have emerged as one of the clubs interested in the 35-year-old defender. According to Gazzetta dello Sport, Milan owner Gerry Cardinale is an admirer of the Dutchman and believes he can make a difference to Ruben Amorim’s project through his experience and technical quality.

Sources indicate that as a result, Evatt has departed the club, confirmed by Blackpool on Thursday afternoon. Evatt was a crucial player for Blackpool when they went from League One to the Premier League just over a decade ago, making over 250 appearances.

Gary Rowett brings substantial Championship and League One experience and a proven ability to organise and stabilise sides swiftly.

During long spells at Millwall and Birmingham he regularly extracted solid results from squads that were not the strongest in the division, often through compact defensive structures, aggressive pressing and pragmatic game management.

He is tactically flexible rather than wedded to one system and has a track record of improving results mid-season. For a Blackpool side currently near the bottom of League One, his experience of grinding out points and rebuilding confidence would be a clear asset.

Luke Williams’ standout achievement was guiding Notts County to promotion from the National League with a record points total and highly attractive, possession-dominant football. However, he was dismissed by Peterborough United in League One this season.

He builds sides that control games, press effectively and score freely, which could energise the Blackpool support and improve the squad’s technical confidence. He also has experience of the demands of League One and the Championship.

While his recent spells at Swansea and Peterborough were mixed, his proven ability to implement a clear, progressive style and maximise players in a promotion environment makes him a credible candidate to lift Blackpool up the table.

Matt Bloomfield’s strongest case rests on his excellent work at Wycombe, where he turned a mid-table League One side into one of the division’s most competitive teams, regularly challenging near the top while playing energetic, high-intensity football.

Recent findings suggest that he is known for his player-centred approach, clear communication and ability to create a positive culture. Although his subsequent spells at Luton and Oxford were less successful, those were at Championship level.

It has been revealed that in League One he has shown he can overachieve with limited resources, making him an attractive option for Blackpool’s current situation. With Blackpool struggling at the moment, his player-management skills could be crucial to get the club back on track.

Liverpool coach joins Rob Edwards on Swansea City manager radar

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (921 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Co

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Swansea City are on the hunt for a new head coach after Vitor Matos departed for Ligue 1 side Strasbourg, and both Rob Edwards and Tommy Elphick are among the contenders to replace him.
  • The Championship side has yet to formally announce Matos' departure, but the BlueCo-led French outfit confirmed his arrival on Wednesday, with the Swans set to receive around £5 million in compensation for his services.
  • Matos leaves Swansea having taken them from 20th in the second tier upon his arrival midway through last season all the way to the summit in the early stages of the ongoing campaign.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Swansea City are on the hunt for a new head coach after Vitor Matos departed for Ligue 1 side Strasbourg, and both Rob Edwards and Tommy Elphick are among the contenders to replace him.

The Championship side has yet to formally announce Matos' departure, but the BlueCo-led French outfit confirmed his arrival on Wednesday, with the Swans set to receive around £5 million in compensation for his services.

Matos leaves Swansea having taken them from 20th in the second tier upon his arrival midway through last season all the way to the summit in the early stages of the ongoing campaign.

A run of four defeats in five leading up to the November international break saw them drop to sixth, but they're still three points off Birmingham City, who at the moment occupy the top spot.

Now, Swansea have to source someone who can maintain their strong start, as they look to mount a promotion challenge after five consecutive campaigns finishing between 10th and 15th.

According to TalkSPORT's Alex Crook, two of the early candidates to replace Vitor Matos as Swansea boss are former Wolves head coach Rob Edwards and Liverpool coach Tommy Elphick.

Edwards has been out of work since the summer, when he was rather unceremoniously sacked by Wolves following their relegation from the Premier League. He found out the news from social media while he was on holiday, after being one of the driving forces behind the signing of Kieran Trippier and the return of Raul Jimenez.

In the Championship, he has experience at the top end of the table. He took Luton Town up into the Premier League in the 2022/23 campaign, and last season had Middlesbrough battling amongst the automatic promotion places before leaving for Molineux.

He has had his failings at this level, though, such as with Luton following their relegation from the top flight and at Watford for a brief period in 2022, although he isn't the only manager to fall victim to the events at Vicarage Road.

Sources indicate that meanwhile, this isn't the first time that Elphick has been linked with a head coach role at Championship level. The former Bournemouth defender rejected the opportunity to take over at Bristol City during their managerial search during the off-season, instead following Andoni Iraola to form part of his coaching staff at Liverpool.

The 39-year-old has coached ever since his retirement in 2021, being part of the first-team staff at the Vitality Stadium since Gary O'Neil's time at the club in 2022, until he left for Anfield in the summer.

Sources indicate that swansea fans are still stung by Matos' departure and the haste with which it happened. Strasbourg's official approach only took place on Monday, with this whole ordeal coming quite out of the blue.

Recent findings suggest that those at the Swansea.com Stadium had become admirers of the football being played under the Portuguese boss, playing high-intensity, pressing football while also being good in possession, too. Replacing him will be difficult, and supporters online aren't enamoured by the reports linking their post with Edwards and Elphick.

The majority of the discourse is coming Edwards' way, though.

The 43-year-old isn't seen as an inspiring choice, even despite his relative success at Championship level, and some Swans fans don't think he'd be able to oversee a smooth transition from the football seen under Matos.

"Don’t particularly want us to go down the Rob Edwards route to be honest, as I’m not convinced he’s the right fit for us in terms of style of play," one fan said in response to the reports.

In a recent development, "If it is Rob Edwards I'd be extremely disappointed. Would undo all the good work we've done over the last year," another mentioned, while a third commented, "It’s just so underwhelming, isn’t it?".

Even one fan commented, "Rob Edwards, no, Tommy Elphick, yes," indicating that they'd rather have someone who hasn't been a head coach yet in his career over Edwards at this stage of the season.

In a recent development, swansea went against the grain and took a risk with hiring Matos back in November last year. The then-37-year-old was incredibly inexperienced as a main dugout man, taking charge of 12 games for Portuguese side Maritimo before heading to South Wales.

Especially with the club being advised by Jamestown Analytics now, the data company founded by Brighton and Hove Albion owner Tony Bloom, perhaps it should be expected that Matos' replacement will equally be out of left-field, if the data can advise manager hires, that is.

Elphick seems destined to become a head coach someday, with him learning under one of the best up-and-coming bosses in the English game right now, in Iraola, and his time at Liverpool will expose him to coaching better players against elite opposition both domestically and in Europe.

It has been revealed that who do you think Swansea City will hire to replace Vitor Matos? Let us know in the comments.

It's also worth noting that there's an easy comparison between Matos and Elphick, not just in their relative managerial inexperience, but also in the fact that they've spent time at Anfield in the dugout, with the now-Strasbourg head coach learning under Jürgen Klopp for nearly five years.

It will be interesting to see where Swansea go from Matos; whether they'll hire someone more well-known who could maintain play-off form, or if they bring in someone to help grow with them, like they did this time last year.

Mauricio Pochettino is preparing to make several changes to his Manchester United squad, with the defence expected to be a major priority over the coming transfer windows.

Noussair Mazraoui is among those whose long-term future at Old Trafford remains uncertain, despite previously being highly regarded by the club.

The Argentine is keen to assess the Morocco international in person before deciding whether to make a new contract a priority.

Mazraoui is attracting interest from clubs in both Italy and Saudi Arabia, but Pochettino wants to take a closer look at the right-back over the coming weeks before reaching a verdict on his future, according to new reports.

The 29-year-old is contracted to United until the summer of 2028, with the club also holding an option to extend his deal by a further year.

Consequently, neither party is in immediate danger of running out of time to agree fresh terms, and there is no urgency to conclude negotiations.

However, Mazraoui has endured an injury-disrupted start to the campaign, making just five Premier League appearances so far.

United are understood to be planning a 'defensive overhaul' across the next few transfer windows, although the former Bayern Munich defender could avoid the significant changes expected elsewhere in the backline.

His versatility is a major asset, having featured at right-back, left-back and centre-back, while he remains viewed as a potentially notable part of the project at Old Trafford.

Nevertheless, Mazraoui will need to impress Pochettino before the manager decides whether to commit to him for the longer term.

United's defensive problems have plagued the club for several seasons, and simply making one or two adjustments is unlikely to provide the necessary solution.

Pochettino, therefore, needs to take a wider view of the backline, with multiple additions potentially required across the defensive positions.

Left-back should be a particularly notable area of focus, while further reinforcements at centre-back and right-back could also be needed depending on who survives the anticipated overhaul.

Mazraoui's ability to cover several positions could make him a useful squad member, but his injury record and contract situation mean that his future cannot be taken for granted.

Ultimately, Pochettino must establish which defenders can form part of his long-term looks before United commit significant resources to rebuilding their defence.

Luke Graham seizes his chance to shine in Scotland back-line... now Stoke defender aims to make himself a fixture for years to come

📅 14 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 6 min read (1120 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dailymail

📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.
  • Published: 17:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026.
  • Whatever concerns there may legitimately be about the limited progress seen in Sebastien Pocognoli’s brief time in charge of Scotland, the Belgian has hardly been blessed with good fortune.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By JOHN MCGARRY, SCOTTISH CHIEF SPORTS FEATURE WRITER.

Published: 17:30 EST, 14 November 2026 | Updated: 18:01 EST, 14 November 2026.

Whatever concerns there may legitimately be about the limited progress seen in Sebastien Pocognoli’s brief time in charge of Scotland, the Belgian has hardly been blessed with good fortune.

In five matches to date in the Nations League, the manager has not yet been able to select the same back-three in two consecutive outings. Injuries and suspensions have seen to that.

For all that, you sense that even if he’d had a full quota of players to choose from, Pocognoli would still be figuring out his preferred defensive grouping.

Recent findings suggest that this does feel like a time of opportunity for those who are fresh on the scene. Catch the eye and there’s a real chance to become established as a mainstay of the team moving forward.

Luke Graham did his chances of doing just that no harm at all in his first start and second cap for his country on Friday.

Playing in between Ryan Porteous and Kieran Tierney, the Stoke City man made a compelling case to stay there with a strong and diligent display.

Luke Graham enjoyed a composed debut for Scotland as they recorded a much-needed win.

On the back of a summer move from Dundee to the English Championship, Graham appears to have taken the step-up to international level in his stride.

‘It’s something I’ve always wanted to do since I was growing up, so I have to be ready for the moment and take it when it comes,’ he stated.

According to recent reports, ‘I think there’s good competition. We have a lot of good centre-halves. Obviously, it was unfortunate for Welshy (Stephen Welsh) and Binksy (Luis Binks) to go out with injury, but that opens up a space for me to come in and try to cement a place.

‘When you’re out on that pitch, you have to do everything you can to try and stay in the team. I gave my all and I’ll just need to wait and see what happens going forward.’.

Timing can be vital in football. And it’s conceivable that Graham’s might just propel him to become a Scotland regular.

While playing at Dens Park saw him mentioned in dispatches with regards to a call-up, his move to England, coming just before Pocognoli was revealed as Steve Clarke’s successor, has seen his dream rapidly become reality.

‘I’ve always remarked that one thing I wanted to do in my career was play for Scotland, so to get it over the line was pretty special,’ he reflected.

Former Dundee defender Graham proudly belts out the national anthem ahead of kick-off.

‘Not much is going wrong for me at the moment, so it’s just about maintaining that and keeping it going every week.

‘I wouldn’t say I merited a start as we have a lot of good players in the camp. It’s up to the manager to pick the team and, luckily, he gave me the chance.

‘He just stated to go out and enjoy it and do what you’re doing every week at Stoke. I think I did all right.’.

Notwithstanding how limited the North Macedonians were on the night, Pocognoli was entitled to take encouragement from the way the back three acquitted themselves.

Industry observers note that playing closer to each other than we’d seen in the previous matches, they were rarely unpicked by balls through the middle. Angus Gunn was not overworked in goal. Tellingly, the only concession of the night came when Scott McTominay lost his man at a corner.

It has been revealed that ‘I think a lot of it is just being brave,’ Graham reflected. ‘It’s about bravery in going man-to-man with the striker, being brave on the ball, trying to break the lines and keeping possession.

‘So, I think bravery is the main thing and concentration as well.’.

Graham keeps a close eye on North Macedonian danger man Elmin Rastoder at Hampden.

In a recent development, with the defence solid enough, Pocognoli had a platform for a much-needed win. While the narrow scoreline made the final moments more anxious than they should have been, on balance, Scotland were deserved winners.

‘It’s just about winning games at this stage of the competition, so that was good,’ mentioned Graham. ‘I think, if I’m being harsh, we should have killed the game off before it got to 1-1. We had a few good chances to put them to bed.

It has been revealed that ‘Then we kinda shot ourselves in the foot by conceding from a set piece. But Ben Gannon-Doak does well for the penalty and for us to go 2-1 up and see it out was good.’.

No one would dispute that the display was a long way from perfect. There’s significant room for improvement ahead of the concluding group match with Switzerland on Monday.

‘We’re going through a bit of a transitional spell at the minute, so it’s not going to be all smooth sailing from the get-go,’ Graham noted. ‘It’s about adjusting and trying to build on performances in every game. I think it’s going to take time.

‘It’s a different style, a different manager and we just have to keep being patient. You look at the squad now and there’s a lot of fresh, young players coming through. It’s just about encouraging us young boys and showing we can get a place in the squad.

‘It is going to take time but, once we get there, we’re going to do really well and compete right at the top of the game.’.

Graham has been a huge success in Stoke's flying start to the Championship season.

Industry observers note that graham does look like he’s moving in the right direction. From watching Scotland compete at the World Cup on licensed premises five months ago, he hopes he too can be the toast of the nation one day.

Recent findings suggest that ‘I didn’t go. It was too expensive for me,’ he explained. ‘I think I was just like everyone else, watching in the pub with their mates. It was pretty amazing and hopefully I can be part of something like that one day.

‘I wasn’t too far away (previously), I think. Steve Clarke, the former manager, told me that. It’s just about trusting myself now and hopefully getting there one day.

It has been revealed that ‘There’s been a lot of hard work and dedication which has led me to this point. I’m very grateful to a lot of people who have helped me in my career so far and just to get this chance is amazing.’.
