📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Martyn Waghorn believes the Derby County senior leaders could have done more to prevent the car crash that left captain Richard Keogh injured during his time at the club.

Sources indicate that the incident occurred in September 2019, following a Derby County team-bonding evening which began with bowling and continued at the Joiners Arms pub. A small group, including captain Richard Keogh, stayed drinking into the night, per The Guardian.

It has been revealed that tom Lawrence subsequently crashed his Range Rover into the back of Mason Bennett's Mercedes before hitting a lamppost, with Keogh unconscious in the back. Both Lawrence and Bennett were over the drink-drive limit and initially left the scene. Keogh suffered serious knee ligament damage, facing around 15 months out.

According to the report in The Guardian, the controversy deepened when Derby sacked Keogh for gross misconduct, although he later won £2.3 million in compensation.

However, Martyn Waghorn believes more could have been done to prevent the incident altogether during his interview with BBC Sport Derby, stating: "We can't get away from the fact that it's completely unacceptable.

"I don't know the full ins and outs, [but he (Richard Keogh) was scapegoated, wasn't he?] Yeah, he was.This is really difficult for me.

What do you make of Waghorn's statement? Comment below!

"He shouldn't have been sacked the way he was so abruptly, but I understand the decision. In the long-term, as a senior leader, I think he could have had a bit more of a say in terms of no, let's not do this.

Industry observers note that "You're the captain of the football club. Taxis are not far away. We can easily sort something out. I just feel some senior figures could have done more to prevent the situation and it was easily preventable.".

Waghorn's statement won't impress everyone but he will mostly be fondly remembered at the club, having enjoyed two spells at Derby, scoring 37 goals in 150 appearances.

He initially joined from Ipswich Town in 2018 after an impressive season, having previously enjoyed a prolific spell at Rangers, where he scored 44 goals in 78 appearances and won the Scottish Championship.

Waghorn was part of Frank Lampard's side that reached the 2019 play-off final and later scored a crucial penalty against Sheffield Wednesday in May 2021 to help Derby avoid relegation.

He returned in 2023, scoring seven goals as Paul Warne's side won promotion from League One. Having done that, he retired from professional football in 2025 after spells at Northampton and Coventry City.

Not everyone connected with Derby County has reacted well to the statement, with one Derby supporter on X stating: "Just another grown man not taking accountability for his actions, nothing newly introduced.".

Another Derby fan said: "Imagine he actually took accountability".

A further reply on X read: "Grown men should have known better plain and simple. Especially when the club captain is involved. Don’t get why post this when things are still a bit fractious at the club at the minute. Poor from you. @BBCDerbySport #dcfc #dcfcfans".

Another reply from an angry Derby fan added: "They’re adults earning thousands of pounds a week, do you really need your captain to book you a taxi?".

Divock Origi has discussed what went wrong during his time at AC Milan, from the injuries to the Rossoneri’s decision to exclude him.

In a recent development, origi joined Milan after the Scudetto season, i.e. the summer of 2022, and the idea was that he would be able to alternate with Olivier Giroud. However, a couple of injuries made his start difficult and it only went downhill from there.

Industry observers note that read SempreMilan ad-free and get access to exclusive news. Click here for a free trial!

Despite making 36 appearances in his first season, he got just two goals and was thus sent out on loan for the next season, joining Nottingham Forest. One goal and one assist later, he returned to Milan, where it was promptly decided that he was no longer part of the project.

Instead of taking the opportunity to continue his career elsewhere, Origi decided to stay and train on his own. His hefty salary of €4m net (€5.24m gross) frustrated Milan and in December 2025, they finally got the striker to terminate his contract six months earlier than its expiration.

Sources indicate that in short, it was a costly deal for Milan and for Origi, the move effectively killed his career. Speaking to the Belgian outlet HLN.be, as cited by MilanPress, the former striker explained what happened and why he then decided to retire (in the summer of 2026).

“At 27, my time at Liverpool was over. Sometimes you need to step out of your comfort zone and take on a newly introduced challenge. It’s the only way to grow as a person. AC Milan was a very interesting project.

Industry observers note that “Paolo Maldini signed me and I felt he truly believed in me. It’s just that I got injured. Usually, I work on my preparation with my personal trainer, but this time it didn’t work. I lost much of my basic fitness; it was difficult.”.

It has been revealed that “I don’t take it personally. It was a professional decision. Was I happy about it? Obviously not. But can I understand it? Yes. I was left out of the squad for a while and wasn’t allowed to train with the first team.

Recent findings suggest that “There was the option of joining the youth team. I can’t say too much about some things for contractual reasons… Let’s just say we weren’t on the same page about it. My experience helped me keep a clear head.

“I was convinced that if you have the right intentions, everything will work out for the best in the end.”.

In a recent development, “I had options in football, but for me it was also a time when I was starting to think about my future away from the sport. Don’t get me wrong, I’ve always dedicated myself body and soul to football. It was my great passion, ” he stated.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Lewis Blain | 18 Nov 2026 07:40.

Liverpool have taken a significant step towards securing Alexis Mac Allister's long-term future by opening contract negotiations with the midfielder.

The Argentina international has been keen to extend his stay at Anfield, but there had been growing frustration over the lack of progress.

However, fresh claims suggest the Reds have finally changed their stance and begun discussions over a new deal.

According to reliable Argentine journalist Cesar Luis Merlo (via Sport Witness), Liverpool have opened negotiations with Mac Allister over a contract extension.

The 27-year-old's current agreement runs until June 2028, meaning the Reds have made an early move to keep him at Anfield beyond that date.

There is no agreement in place yet, and Merlo has not disclosed any proposed salary or contract length, although the coming weeks could provide a clearer indication of whether both parties can reach a compromise.

The development represents a change from the situation described by Mac Allister's father and agent, Carlos, who told ESPN Brazil just days ago that Liverpool had not started negotiations.

The long-serving star has also previously voiced his disappointment at the lack of an offer, admitting in September that he was "very, very sad" about the situation, particularly after teammates Ryan Gravenberch and Dominik Szoboszlai had been offered newly introduced contracts.

More recently, Mac Allister attempted to reassure supporters, expressing hope that the club's board would reconsider its position.

Liverpool's reported change of heart could reflect Mac Allister's importance to Andoni Iraola's prepares, with the £55m enforcer continuing to receive regular opportunities.

Starting eight of the Reds' ten Premier League matches and three of their four Champions League fixtures, he remains a prominent part of the team's midfield setup.

That level of involvement makes it difficult to justify allowing uncertainty over his future to continue, particularly when he has consistently indicated a desire to remain at Anfield.

There is still work to do before an agreement is reached, but opening discussions is an encouraging development for Liverpool.

Mac Allister has made his feelings clear, and the club now appears to be responding. Keeping an established midfielder of his importance could prove a sensible decision as Iraola continues shaping his squad.
